definition_zh: 段落；段；报刊短讯；把……分段
definition_en: a group of sentences that develop one idea, a short separate item in a newspaper, and to divide a piece of writing into such groups
core_image: 一页稿纸上，红笔在句子之间划出几道横线
scene: 编辑把稿子摊在桌上，用红笔在需要停顿的地方画一道线。She moved the last sentence into a new paragraph and read the page again.
sceneCN: 这里 paragraph 是「段落」（第 1 个义项：文章里围绕一个意思的一组句子）；句意为她把最后一句移到新的一段，又把这一页重读了一遍。图中可辨识物件：稿纸、红笔、页边的横线。

derivatives.zh: 由 paragraph 加 -ing 构成，指分段的处理方式或页面上分段的样子
由 paragraph 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，指与段落有关的

senses.title: A group of sentences on one idea
senses.definition: a group of sentences that develop a single idea and are separated from the next group by a line break or an indent
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个意思展开的一组句子，与下一组之间以换行或缩进隔开
senses.example: She moved the last sentence into a new paragraph and read the page again.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最后一句移到新的一段，又把这一页重读了一遍。
senses.why: Greek paragraphos named a stroke written beside a line to mark a break; the mark then gave its name to the block of text it introduced.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 paragraphos 指在文字旁边画出、用来标示停顿的一道笔迹；后来这个记号就指它引出的那一段文字。

senses.title: A short item in a newspaper
senses.definition: a short separate item of news or comment in a newspaper, often only a few sentences long
senses.definitionCN: 报纸上独立成条的一小段新闻或评论，常常只有几句话
senses.example: The local paper ran a short paragraph about the missing cat.
senses.exampleCN: 地方报纸登了一小段关于那只走失的猫的消息。
senses.why: Because the mark cut a page into small blocks, the word could name any small block of print, and news writing soon used it for a brief item.
senses.whyCN: 因为这道记号把页面切成小块，这个词也就能指任何一小块印刷文字，新闻写作很快用它来指一条短讯。

senses.title: To divide writing into paragraphs
senses.definition: to arrange a piece of writing in paragraphs, or to mark the places where new paragraphs begin
senses.definitionCN: 把一篇文字安排成若干段落，或标出另起一段的位置
senses.example: He paragraphed the report carefully so that each claim stood alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他仔细地把报告分段，让每一条主张各占一段。
senses.why: Once the noun named the block, the verb followed by the usual English route: to paragraph is to cut a text into those blocks.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指段落这个块，动词就顺着英语常见的路子跟上来了：paragraph 就是按这些块把文字切开。

intro.en: Paragraph goes back to Greek words for beside and to write; the original thing was a mark in the margin, and the text it introduced borrowed the name.
intro.cn: paragraph 上溯到希腊语中表示「在旁边」与「写」的两个词；最初指的是页边的一个记号，后来它引出的那段文字借用了这个名字。

items.en: Para meant beside, and graphein meant to write or to scratch; a paragraphos was a stroke set beside a line of writing.
items.cn: para 意为在旁边，graphein 意为写、刻画；paragraphos 就是写在文字行旁的一道笔迹。

items.en: The noun came to mean not only the mark but the passage that the mark set off, a shift from sign to the thing signified.
items.cn: 这个名词后来不仅指记号，也指记号所分隔出的那一段文字，是从符号转向所指之物的变化。

items.en: Late Latin paragraphus and French paragraphe carried the term westward as a word of writing, copying and law.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 paragraphus 与法语的 paragraphe 把这个术语向西传播，用于书写、抄录与法律文书。

items.en: English paragraph first named the marginal mark, then the section of text that followed it.
items.cn: 英语里的 paragraph 先指页边的记号，随后指记号之后的那一节文字。

items.en: Modern English uses paragraph for a block of prose, for a short news item, and as a verb for dividing text.
items.cn: 现代英语用 paragraph 指散文中的一段、报刊上的一条短讯，也作动词表示把文字分段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Greek compounds that begin with the same short element, and each one attaches it to a different stem; the near-meaning group gathers other units of written text.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以那个短小成分开头的希腊复合词，但每个词接的词干都不同；近义组收其他表示文本单位的词。

entries.definition: Greek para plus allelos, one another; the two words share a prefix but are separate formations.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 allelos（彼此）；两词前缀写法相同，却是各自独立的构词，不是同一词族。

entries.definition: Para beside plus doxa opinion, a statement that sits against common belief.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 doxa（意见），指与常见看法相左的说法。

entries.definition: Para beside plus phrasis wording, a rewording of a text.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 phrasis（说法），指对原文的改写。

entries.definition: Para beside plus sitos food, one who eats at another person's table.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 sitos（食物），指在别人桌边吃饭的寄生者。

entries.definition: A short section of a book or a speech.
entries.definitionCN: 书或讲话中的一小节。

entries.definition: One of the parts into which a whole is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 整体被分成的部分之一。

entries.definition: A group of words that expresses a complete thought.
entries.definitionCN: 表达一个完整意思的一组词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek compound whose first half means beside; what it originally named was a mark, and English keeps both the mark and the block of text.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语复合词，前半意为「在旁边」；它最初命名的是一个记号，英语至今同时保留记号与那段文字两层意思。

normal.en: The Greek parts are para, beside, and graphein, to write: a paragraph began as a mark written beside the text.
normal.cn: 希腊部件是 para（在旁边）与 graphein（写）：paragraph 原本是写在文字旁边的一道记号。

normal.en: The mark gave its name to the sentences it introduced, which is why the word now means the text block itself.
normal.cn: 这道记号把自己的名字给了它引出的那几句，所以今天这个词指的是文字块本身。

normal.en: Paragraphing is the noun for the way a page is divided, and the -ing form keeps the action in view.
normal.cn: paragraphing 是表示「分段方式」的名词，-ing 形式让动作保持在视野里。

normal.en: The para- in paragraph hooks onto a verb of writing, while the para- in parallel belongs to a word for one another; they look alike but are separate formations.
normal.cn: paragraph 的 para- 接的是表示「写」的动词，parallel 的 para- 接的是表示「彼此」的词；两者看着一样，却是独立的两套构词。

normal.en: A newspaper paragraph is short because it is one small block of print on a crowded page.
normal.cn: 报纸上的 paragraph 之所以短，因为它是拥挤版面上的一小块印刷文字。

abstract.en: A paragraph is a pause made visible: the eye rests where the writer decided to stop.
abstract.cn: 段落是让停顿可见：目光停在作者决定收住的地方。

abstract.en: Cutting a page into blocks lends order to thought before the thought is fully clear.
abstract.cn: 把页面切成块，是在想法还没完全清楚之前先给它一个次序。

abstract.en: Two words can share four letters and still come from different rooms of the same language.
abstract.cn: 两个词可以共用四个字母，却仍来自同一种语言里不同的房间。

examples.en: She moved the last sentence into a new paragraph and read the page again.
examples.cn: 她把最后一句移到新的一段，又把这一页重读了一遍。

examples.en: The local paper ran a short paragraph about the missing cat.
examples.cn: 地方报纸登了一小段关于那只走失的猫的消息。

examples.en: He paragraphed the report carefully so that each claim stood alone.
examples.cn: 他仔细地把报告分段，让每一条主张各占一段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍了个拉夫」——写完一段拍拍手，翻篇再写；记住 paragraph 是段落。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁边）加 graphein（写），paragraphos 原指写在行旁表示停顿的记号，后指记号引出的那段文字，经晚期拉丁语与法语进入英语。它与 parallel 虽然都写作 para-，却是两套各自独立的希腊构词，并非同源词族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a break marked in a text; the senses run from the block of sentences, to a short newspaper item, to the verb for cutting prose into such blocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是文本中被标出的一次停顿；义项从一组句子，走到报刊上的短讯，再到把文字切成这种块的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line drawn down the margin, marking where the reader may pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：页边画下的一道红线，标出读者可以换气的地方。

branches.en: a red stroke in the margin of a manuscript
branches.cn: 手稿页边的一道红线

branches.en: a page where each idea gets its own block
branches.cn: 每个意思各占一块的页面

branches.en: a few lines about a lost cat in the local paper
branches.cn: 地方报纸上关于走失小猫的几行字

branches.en: an editor splitting a long report by hand
branches.cn: 编辑亲手把长报告分段

branches.en: a writer deciding where the reader may breathe
branches.cn: 作者决定读者在哪里换气

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound of a preposition and a verb of writing, filtered through Latin and French, and English adds its own endings to it.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中一个介词与一个「写」的动词拼成的复合词，经拉丁语与法语过滤后进入英语，英语又给它加上自己的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; late Latin paragraphus is itself a borrowing of the Greek noun, and the English word came by way of French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；晚期拉丁语的 paragraphus 本身是对希腊名词的借用，英语词则经由法语传来。

items.meaning: a stroke written beside a line
the way a text is divided
the sign that starts a new paragraph

definition_zh: 平行的；类似的；类似的事物；与……相似；与……同时发生
definition_en: of lines, always the same distance apart and never meeting; similar in important ways; a person or thing resembling another; to be similar to or to happen at the same time as
core_image: 两条铁轨并肩伸向远方，始终不碰在一起
scene: 两条铁轨穿过田野，一直伸到看不见的地方。The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
sceneCN: 这里 parallel 是「平行的」（第 1 个义项：两条线距离处处相同、永不相交）；句意为这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。图中可辨识物件：铁轨、枕木、远处的隧道口。

pos.zh: 类似的事物；可类比的对象

derivatives.zh: 由 parallel 加 -ism 构成，指平行、对应的状态，也指修辞上的排比
由 parallel 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed 构成，指无可比拟的
由 parallel 与希腊语 gramma（线）复合而成，指两组对边分别平行的四边形

senses.title: Always the same distance apart
senses.definition: of two or more lines or surfaces, keeping the same distance apart at every point so that they never meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条或多条线、面的距离处处相等，因而永不相交
senses.example: The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。
senses.why: Greek parallelos joins para, beside, with allelos, one another: two things set beside each other with an unbroken gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 parallelos 由 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此）拼成：两样东西彼此并排，中间隔着一道始终不变的距离。

senses.title: Similar in important ways
senses.definition: similar in a way that allows one thing to be compared with another, especially in structure or development
senses.definitionCN: 在结构或发展上相似到可以彼此对照
senses.example: The two cities followed parallel paths of growth after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后这两座城市走上了相似的发展道路。
senses.why: Lines that never meet still hold a constant relation, so the word came to name things that move in step without ever touching.
senses.whyCN: 永不相交的线仍保持固定的关系，于是这个词也用来指那些同步前进、却从不接触的事物。

senses.title: A person or thing like another
senses.titleCN: 类似的事物；可类比的对象
senses.definition: a person, event or situation that can be compared with another because of a clear resemblance
senses.definitionCN: 因为明显相像而可以拿来与另一者比较的人、事件或处境
senses.example: Historians drew a parallel between the two collapses.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这两次崩塌放在一起比较。
senses.why: Once the adjective names resemblance, the noun can name the second item itself, giving speakers a way to say that one thing is another's counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦表示相似，名词就能指那第二个对象本身，让人可以直说一件事是另一件事的对应物。

senses.title: To be similar to or happen alongside
senses.definition: to be similar to something, or to happen at the same time and in a connected way
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相似，或与它同时发生并彼此关联
senses.example: The rise in rents paralleled the growth of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨与这座城市的发展同步发生。
senses.why: The verb sets that picture in motion: two courses of events keep the same gap and move forward together.
senses.whyCN: 动词把那幅画面变成运动：两条事态的线索保持同样的间距，一起向前推进。

intro.en: Parallel comes from a Greek adjective meaning beside one another, built for geometry and later borrowed into Latin and English as a term of lines and likeness.
intro.cn: parallel 来自一个意为「彼此并排」的希腊形容词，本为几何学而造，后来被拉丁语与英语借用，用来指线与相似。

items.en: Parallelos joined para, beside, with allelos, one another, and described things set side by side at an even distance.
items.cn: parallelos 把 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此）拼在一起，描述以相等距离并排摆放的东西。

items.en: Greek geometers used the word for straight lines in one plane that never meet, and this technical sense has never been lost.
items.cn: 希腊几何学家用这个词指同一平面内永不相交的直线，这一专业义至今没有丢失。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as parallelus; it was a learned borrowing rather than a word inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 parallelus；这是学术借用，不是从拉丁语本土传下的词。

items.en: English took the word by way of Latin and French, first for geometry and soon after for any two things that resemble each other.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁语与法语借入这个词，先用于几何，随后很快用于任何彼此相像的两样东西。

items.en: Modern English keeps the geometrical sense, adds similarity and events running side by side, and uses the noun for a counterpart.
items.cn: 现代英语保留几何义，增加了相似与并行发生的意思，并用名词形式指对应物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other Greek compounds that begin with the same short element, each built on a different stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for likeness and for a matching thing.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以同一个短小成分开头的希腊复合词，每个词接的词干都不同；近义组收表示相似以及对应物的词。

entries.definition: Greek para plus graphein, to write; the prefix looks the same but the formation is separate, not a shared family.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 graphein（写）；前缀写法相同，但构词各自独立，不是同一词族。

entries.definition: Para beside plus doxa opinion, a claim that runs against common belief.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 doxa（意见），指违背常见看法的说法。

entries.definition: Para beside plus sitos food, one who eats at another person's table.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 sitos（食物），指在别人桌边吃饭的寄生者。

entries.definition: Greek para plus allassein, to change; it shares the all- element with parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 allassein（改变）；与 parallel 共享 all- 这一成分。

entries.definition: Almost the same, but not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎相同，但并不完全一样。

entries.definition: Similar in a way that allows a comparison between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 相似到可以把两者放在一起比较。

entries.definition: A person or thing that has the same role as another elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处担任同一角色的人或事物。

entries.definition: Next to and parallel with something.
entries.definitionCN: 在旁边并与某物并排。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek picture of two things laid side by side, and the whole family keeps the ideas of even distance, likeness and a matching partner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语里两样东西并排放置的画面，整族词都带着等距、相似与配对这三层意思。

normal.en: The Greek parts are para, beside, and allelos, one another, so parallel lines are lines placed beside each other.
normal.cn: 希腊部件是 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此），所以平行线就是彼此并排放着的线。

normal.en: The same picture yields the sense of similar: two courses stay side by side without ever meeting.
normal.cn: 同一幅画面也生出「相似」：两条走向并排前进，却始终不相交。

normal.en: Parallel ends in -el with one r, while parallelism adds -ism and keeps the same l-sound.
normal.cn: parallel 以一个 r、结尾 -el 拼写，parallelism 则加 -ism，l 音不变。

normal.en: In parallel means two things are running at the same time, like two tracks carrying trains.
normal.cn: in parallel 指两件事同时进行，就像两条各跑列车的轨道。

normal.en: The verb is regular: parallels, paralleled, paralleling, with the final l doubled.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：parallels、paralleled、paralleling，末尾的 l 双写。

abstract.en: Parallel lines are a promise that two things can stay close forever without ever becoming one.
abstract.cn: 平行线是一种承诺：两样东西可以永远靠得很近，却始终不合成一个。

abstract.en: To draw a parallel is to say that two separate stories are running on the same track.
abstract.cn: 把两者作类比，就是说两个互不相干的故事跑在同一条轨道上。

abstract.en: A parallel universe is the everyday metaphor for a life that kept the same distance from this one.
abstract.cn: 平行宇宙是日常语言里对「另一种人生」的比喻：它与这一种人生始终隔着同样的距离。

examples.en: The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
examples.cn: 这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。

examples.en: The two cities followed parallel paths of growth after the war.
examples.cn: 战后这两座城市走上了相似的发展道路。

examples.en: The rise in rents paralleled the growth of the city.
examples.cn: 租金的上涨与这座城市的发展同步发生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「排啊排」——两条线一直排着走，谁也不碰谁；记住 parallel 是平行。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁边）加 allelos（彼此）构成 parallelos，指彼此并排、距离相等的线；经中世纪拉丁语 parallelus 与法语进入英语。它与 paragraph 虽然同写 para-，但接的词干不同，是两套独立的构词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things laid side by side at a fixed distance; the senses move from geometry to resemblance, to a matching partner, and to events that run alongside each other.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是以固定距离并排放置的两样东西；义项从几何走到相似，再到对应物，最后是并行发生的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rails shining toward a tunnel mouth, never touching.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条铁轨闪着光伸向隧道口，始终不相碰。

branches.cn: 两条铁轨亮着伸向隧道口

branches.en: two trains holding the same gap on twin tracks
branches.cn: 两列火车在平行轨道上保持同样的间距

branches.en: two cities growing along the same pattern
branches.cn: 两座城市沿同样的模式生长

branches.cn: 历史学家把两次崩塌并排比较

branches.en: rents and population climbing together on a chart
branches.cn: 租金与人口在图表上一同上升

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound of a preposition and a pronoun meaning one another, and English suffixes then build the nouns and adjectives around it.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中一个介词与意为「彼此」的代词拼成的复合词，英语后缀随后在它周围造出名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; medieval Latin parallelus is a learned borrowing of the Greek adjective, so the Latin form follows the Greek rather than feeding it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；中世纪拉丁语的 parallelus 是对希腊形容词的学术借用，拉丁形式是跟着希腊语走的，而非其来源。

items.meaningCN: 两组对边平行的四边形

definition_zh: 包裹；邮包；一块土地；把……包起来；分派
definition_en: something wrapped in paper or packed in a box and sent by post, a measured area of land, or to wrap goods and divide them into portions
core_image: 柜台上一只牛皮纸包被麻绳捆成十字，收件地址写在正面
scene: 邮局柜台前，店员把一只用麻绳捆好的纸包推过来，又把票据压在下面。He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
sceneCN: 这里的 parcel 是「包裹、邮包」（第 1 个义项：包好待寄送的东西）；句意是他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。图中可辨识物件：麻绳、牛皮纸包、票据。

senses.title: Something wrapped and sent by post
senses.definition: something wrapped in paper, tied with string or packed in a box, especially for sending by post
senses.definitionCN: 用纸包好、用绳捆上或装进盒子，尤指通过邮局寄送的东西
senses.example: He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
senses.exampleCN: 他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。
senses.why: Parcel began as Latin particula, a small part, and French used it for a small piece of anything; an item tied up for the post was simply one such piece.
senses.whyCN: parcel 最初是拉丁语 particula，意为「一小部分」，法语用它指任何东西的一小块；寄送时捆好的那件东西，不过是这样的「一块」而已。

senses.title: A measured piece of land
senses.definition: a piece of land, especially one marked out for a particular use or owned as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 一块土地，尤指划作某种用途或作为一个单位拥有的地块
senses.example: They bought a small parcel of land beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边买下了一小块地。
senses.why: If a parcel is a portion cut from a whole, land can be divided the same way, so the word came to name one plot marked on a surveyor's map.
senses.whyCN: 既然 parcel 是从整体里切出的一份，土地也能这样切分，于是这个词用来指测量图上标好的一个地块。

senses.title: To wrap something up
senses.definition: to wrap goods in paper or another material and fasten them, often before sending
senses.definitionCN: 把货物用纸或其他材料包好并捆紧，通常是为了寄送
senses.example: She parcelled the books and took them to the post office.
senses.exampleCN: 她把书包好，送到邮局去。
senses.why: The noun named the finished bundle, so the verb simply names the act of producing it: to parcel is to turn loose goods into one tied package.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是包好的成品，动词便直接指做出这个成品的动作：parcel 就是把散着的东西变成一只捆好的包。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.definition: to divide something into portions and give them out, usually in the phrase parcel out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份分发出去，通常用于 parcel out 这一说法
senses.example: The land was parcelled out among the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地被分给了村民们。
senses.why: Because the word already meant a portion, parcel out reverses the picture: instead of gathering things into one bundle, it cuts the whole into separate shares.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就指「一份」，parcel out 于是把画面翻了过来：不再把东西收进一只包，而是把整体切成一份份拿出去。

intro.en: Parcel comes from Old French parcelle, a small piece, which is a diminutive of Latin particula, itself a small form of pars, part; English first used it for a portion and only later for a package and a plot of land.
intro.cn: parcel 来自古法语 parcelle（一小块），它是拉丁语 particula 的指小形式，而 particula 又是 pars（部分）的小称；英语先用它指「一份」，后来才指包裹与地块。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and it is the ultimate source of a whole family of English words about portions.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，是英语中一整族表示「份」的词的最终来源。

items.en: Particula was the small form of pars, so it named a little part or a tiny piece of something.
items.cn: particula 是 pars 的小称，指一小部分或某物的一小块。

items.en: Old French kept the word as parcelle and used it for a small piece or a portion of a larger whole.
items.cn: 古法语把它保留为 parcelle，用来指一小块或整体中的一份。

items.en: Middle English parcel first meant a part or a portion, and it could name a piece of land as well as a share of goods.
items.cn: 中古英语的 parcel 最初指部分或一份，既能指一块地，也能指一份货物。

items.en: Modern English made the wrapped item the main sense, kept the land sense, and added the verb meanings of wrapping and dividing.
items.cn: 现代英语把包好的东西变成主要义项，保留土地义，又添上「包起来」与「分成份」两个动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin root for part, so the split between parcel and the partial family is visible; the near-meaning group gathers words for wrapped goods.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「部分」词根上的词，方便看清 parcel 与 partial 一族的分叉；近义组收表示包好的货物的词。

normalIntro.en: Parcel is a word for a piece cut from a whole, and its hooks follow that piece from a share of land to a bundle tied for the post.
normalIntro.cn: parcel 是一个表示「从整体中切下的一块」的词，记忆钩子顺着这块东西，从一份土地走到捆好待寄的包裹。

normal.en: Parcel descends from Latin pars, part, through particula and Old French parcelle, so a parcel is literally a little part.
normal.cn: parcel 经由 particula 与古法语 parcelle 上溯拉丁语 pars（部分），所以它字面上就是「一小块」。

normal.en: A parcel of land keeps the oldest sense visible: a measured share of ground, not a thing you mail.
normal.cn: a parcel of land 保留了最古老的义项：量好的一份地，而不是寄出去的东西。

normal.en: Parcel out reverses the picture of a tied bundle: the whole is cut into portions instead of being gathered into one.
normal.cn: parcel out 把捆成一只包的画面翻了过来：整体被切成若干份，而不是被收进一只包。

normal.en: Part and parcel uses the old sense of a share to say that something is an inseparable piece of a larger thing.
normal.cn: part and parcel 用的是「一份」的旧义，表示某物是更大整体中不可分割的一块。

normal.en: The British verb doubles the l as parcelled, while the American spelling keeps one l as parceled.
normal.cn: 英式动词双写 l 写作 parcelled，美式拼写只留一个 l，写作 parceled。

abstract.en: A word that means both a mailed package and a plot of land suggests that owning and sending are both matters of pieces.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指邮寄的包裹又指一块地，说明拥有与投递都与「份」有关。

abstract.en: Because parcel began as a small part, every parcel still carries the idea of a whole that has been divided.
abstract.cn: 因为 parcel 起初指一小部分，所以每一只包裹至今都带着「整体被分割过」的意思。

abstract.en: To parcel out land or money is to admit that a whole cannot stay whole once it belongs to several people.
abstract.cn: 把土地或钱分派出去，等于承认整体一旦归几个人所有，就再也无法保持完整。

senses.title: A national lawmaking assembly
senses.definition: the supreme lawmaking body of a state, especially where the executive answers to it
senses.definitionCN: 一国的最高立法机构，尤指行政须向它负责的体制
senses.example: Parliament debated the bill until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 议会辩论该法案直到午夜。
senses.why: The word first meant a talking together, and the national assembly is the place where the talking decides law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「一起说话」，而国家议会就是说话决定法律的地方。

senses.title: The building
senses.definition: the building or chamber where the assembly meets
senses.definitionCN: 议会开会所在的建筑或议事厅
senses.example: A crowd gathered outside parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 一群人聚集在议会大厦外。
senses.why: By metonymy the place takes the name of the body that meets in it.
senses.whyCN: 借代作用使地点取得了在其中开会之机构的名字。

senses.title: The members collectively
senses.definition: the assembled members considered as one actor
senses.definitionCN: 把全体议员视为一个行动者
senses.example: Parliament was divided on the question.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在这个问题上意见分裂。
senses.why: A body acts through votes, so the name passes from the institution to the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 机构通过投票行动，于是名称从制度转到里面的人。

senses.title: A term or session
senses.definition: the period between one general election and the next, or a single session
senses.definitionCN: 两次大选之间的一段时期，或一次会期
senses.example: The law was passed in the last parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律在上一届议会任期内通过。
senses.why: Because the assembly is dissolved and reconstituted, the word also counts the periods of its life.
senses.whyCN: 由于议会被解散又重新组成，这个词也用来数它生命的周期。

senses.title: A medieval council
senses.titleCN: 中世纪由君主召集的会议
senses.definition: a conference of nobles and clergy summoned by a monarch to advise and consent
senses.definitionCN: 由君主召集、由贵族与教士提供建议并同意的会议
senses.example: The medieval parliament began as a royal council.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的议会起初是王室会议。
senses.why: Before it made law, the assembly was a speaking-together called by the king, and that is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 在制定法律之前，这个集会是由国王召集的「一起说话」，那是最老的义项。

senses.title: A regional or supranational parliament
senses.definition: a lawmaking or deliberative assembly below or above the national level
senses.definitionCN: 低于或高于国家层级的立法或议事议会
senses.example: The Scottish Parliament sits in Edinburgh.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰议会设在爱丁堡。
senses.why: Once the model exists, it can be copied at any level, from a province to a continent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了这个模式，它就能被复制到任何层级，从一省到一洲。

senses.title: Any deliberative assembly
senses.definition: an extended use for a meeting that argues out a decision
senses.definitionCN: 引申用法，指通过争论作出决定的会议
senses.example: The students held a parliament on the library steps.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在图书馆台阶上开了一场议事会。
senses.why: Talking toward a decision is the original action, so the label travels to any group that does it.
senses.whyCN: 为了决定而说话是原本的动作，因此这个标签能转到任何这样做的群体。

senses.title: A literary gathering
senses.titleCN: 文学中的群鸟议事（典故）
senses.definition: the title word of medieval poems in which birds or beasts hold a council
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪诗题中的用词，写群鸟或群兽开会
senses.example: Chaucer's poem is known as the Parliament of Fowls.
senses.exampleCN: 乔叟那首诗被称为《百鸟议会》。
senses.why: The poem takes the assembly's name and applies it to birds, which is the word's most playful reach.
senses.whyCN: 这首诗借用了议会的名字，把它用在鸟身上，是这个词汇最俏皮的延伸。

intro.en: Parliament comes from Old French parlement, first 'a speaking, talk' and then 'a conference'. The verb parler 'to speak' goes back through Late Latin parabolare to parabola 'speech, comparison', from Greek parabole.
intro.cn: parliament 来自古法语 parlement，最初意为「说话、谈话」，后指「会议」。动词 parler「说话」经晚期拉丁 parabolare 上溯到 parabola「言语、比较」，再上溯到希腊语 parabole。

items.en: Parabole meant a placing beside, hence a comparison and a story used as a comparison. It passed into Latin as parabola.
items.cn: parabole 意为「放在旁边」，因此指比较，也指用作比较的故事。它进入拉丁语作 parabola。

items.en: The verb parabolare 'to speak, talk' grew out of parabola in late and vulgar Latin, and from it came French parler.
items.cn: 动词 parabolare「说话、谈话」在晚期与通俗拉丁语中由 parabola 长出，法语 parler 即由此而来。

items.en: Parlement named a speaking or a conference before it named an institution; the Anglo-Latin form parliamentum is recorded from the early thirteenth century.
items.cn: parlement 先指说话或会谈，后指机构；其盎格鲁拉丁形式 parliamentum 自十三世纪早期见于记录。

items.en: English parliament is recorded about 1300 for a formal conference, and by the mid-fourteenth century for the representative assembly of England.
items.cn: 英语 parliament 约在 1300 年指正式会议，到十四世纪中期指英格兰的代表性议会。

items.en: The spelling was altered about 1400 to match Medieval Latin parliamentum, which is why the word has an i that the French form lacks.
items.cn: 拼写约在 1400 年按中世纪拉丁 parliamentum 改动，这就是为什么这个词有一个法语形式所无的 i。

items.en: The chain from Greek parabole is clear. Only the earliest citation of each English sense is approximate, so no source is marked uncertain.
items.cn: 从希腊 parabole 以来的链条清楚。只有各英语义项的最早书证是约数，因此没有需要标为来源不确定的部分。

note.cn: 第一组是同出 parliament 背后「说话」词根的词；第二组是同样以辩论作决定的其他集会。

entries.definition: A conference with an enemy, from the same French verb; it is a talk, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指与敌方的会谈，出自同一个法语动词；它是一次谈话，不是机构。

entries.definition: A sitting room for conversation; the old sense of a room set apart for talking survives here.

entries.definition: A prisoner's promise of good behaviour, literally a word given; it comes through the same speaking root.

entries.definitionCN: 指用来说明道理的短故事，直接来自希腊 parabole；parliament 的词根是由这个名词长出的说话动词。

entries.definition: A national legislature, especially the American one; its image is people coming together, not people speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家立法机关，尤指美国国会；其意象是人走到一起，而非人说话。

entries.definition: The general term for a lawmaking body; parliament is the specific model in which the executive sits inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指立法机关的通用说法；parliament 是行政也坐在其中的特定模式。

entries.definition: Any gathering of people, including a lawmaking one; it is the broad noun that parliament narrows.

entries.definition: The name of certain historical assemblies, as in the Diet of Worms; the word came from a day's appointed meeting.

definition_zh: 部分的；不完全的；偏袒的；偏爱的
definition_en: covering only a part of something and not the whole, favouring one person or side unfairly, or, in the phrase be partial to, liking something very much
core_image: 一面墙只刷了一半，另一半还留着旧漆的颜色
scene: 画廊的墙上挂着一幅被烟熏过的旧画，右半边颜色已经褪去。The restorer could only see a partial view of the original painting.
sceneCN: 这里的 partial 是「部分的、不完全的」（第 1 个义项：只涉及整体的一部分）；句意为修复师只能看到原画的一个局部。图中可辨识物件：旧画、熏痕、褪色的半边。

pos.zh: 部分的；不完全的；偏袒的；偏爱的

derivatives.zh: 由 partial 加 -ly 构成，义为「部分地；不完全地」
由 partial 加 -ity 构成，义为「偏袒；偏爱」

senses.title: Covering only a part
senses.definition: covering or affecting only a part of something, not the whole
senses.definitionCN: 只覆盖或影响某物的一部分，而不是整体
senses.example: The restorer could only see a partial view of the original painting.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师只能看到原画的一个局部。
senses.why: Partial is an adjective built on part, so it describes whatever holds only some of a whole, and the missing remainder is felt in the word itself.
senses.whyCN: partial 是建立在 part 之上的形容词，所以它描述只占整体一部分的东西，词里本身就带着「还缺一部分」的感觉。

senses.title: Favouring one side unfairly
senses.definition: supporting one person, group or side more than another, especially in a way that is unfair
senses.definitionCN: 对人、群体或一方给予更多支持，尤指以不公平的方式
senses.example: The referee was accused of being partial to the home team.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判被指责偏袒主队。
senses.why: If you take only one part of a dispute, you no longer stand above the whole; the word for a part becomes the word for taking sides.
senses.whyCN: 在一场争执里只取其中一部分，人就不再站在整体的上方；于是「部分」这个词变成了「站到一边」的意思。

senses.title: Fond of something
senses.definition: liking a thing or a person very much, used in the phrase be partial to
senses.definitionCN: 非常喜欢某物或某人，用于 be partial to 这一说法
senses.example: She is partial to strong coffee in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她早上偏爱浓咖啡。
senses.why: Liking something is a mild form of favouring it, so the same adjective moves from courts and referees to the breakfast table without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 喜欢某样东西，是「偏向」的温和形式，于是同一个形容词从法庭与球场走到了早餐桌上，形状丝毫未变。

intro.en: Partial comes from Latin partialis, an adjective from pars, part; French passed it to English as parcial, where it first meant belonging to a part and later meant favouring one side.
intro.cn: partial 来自拉丁语 partialis，是 pars（部分）派生的形容词；法语把它写作 parcial 传给英语，先指「属于某一部分的」，后指「偏向一方的」。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and its adjective partialis described whatever belonged to only one part.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，其形容词 partialis 描述只属于某一部分的东西。

items.en: Partialis named what is divided or one-sided, and it could already describe a person who takes a side.
items.cn: partialis 指被分开的或偏向一边的，已经能形容站到某一边的人。

items.en: Old French kept the word as parcial, meaning belonging to a part or showing favour to one side.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 parcial，意为属于一部分的，或对一方表示偏袒的。

items.en: Middle English partial kept both the idea of an incomplete whole and the idea of an unfair preference.
items.cn: 中古英语的 partial 同时保留「整体不完整」与「偏好不公平」两层意思。

items.en: Modern English adds the polite phrase be partial to for liking something, and pairs partial with impartial for fair judgement.
items.cn: 现代英语添上表示喜欢的客气说法 be partial to，又用 impartial 与 partial 相对，表示公正的判断。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the part family side by side so the split between partial, partly and particular is clear; the near-meaning group gathers words for incomplete and for biased.
note.cn: 形近组把 part 一族并排摆开，好让 partial、partly 与 particular 的分叉一目了然；近义组收表示「不完整」与「有偏向」的词。

entries.definition: In some measure but not completely; the adverb built directly on part.
entries.definitionCN: 在某种程度上但不完全；直接由 part 构成的副词。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; from the small form of Latin pars.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；出自拉丁语 pars 的小称。

entries.definition: One specific item or quality rather than any other; from the same small form of pars.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的某一项或某种性质；出自同一小称词。

entries.definition: A wrapped package or a plot of land, also from Latin particula.

entries.definition: Not finished or not having all its parts.

entries.definition: Unfairly favouring one side over another.

entries.definition: Showing only one point of view, or unfair to one party.

entries.definition: Giving an advantage to one person or group.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人或某群体优待的。

normalIntro.en: Partial keeps the shape of part plus a Latin adjective ending, so its hooks show how a piece of a whole turns into a biased choice and then into a quiet liking.
normalIntro.cn: partial 保留着 part 加拉丁形容词词尾的形状，记忆钩子展示「整体的一块」如何变成「偏向的选择」，再变成「含蓄的喜欢」。

normal.en: Partial is part with an adjective ending, so it always suggests that a remainder is missing.
normal.cn: partial 就是 part 加形容词词尾，所以它总暗示还差着一部分。

normal.en: Partly is the adverb for the same idea, while partial is the adjective; a partial success is the thing, and the plan partly worked is the action.
normal.cn: partly 是同一想法的副词，partial 是形容词；partial success 说的是那件事，the plan partly worked 说的是进展。

normal.en: Particular comes from the same small piece of Latin but points to one identified item, not to a fraction of it.
normal.cn: particular 出自同一个「小块」，但指的是一件被认定的东西，而不是它的一部分。

normal.en: Impartial adds the negative prefix im-, so an impartial judge has no part in the argument at all.
normal.cn: impartial 加上否定前缀 im-，所以公正的法官在争执中不属于任何一边。

normal.en: Be partial to is a gentle way of saying you like something, as if you were admitting a small preference.
normal.cn: be partial to 是说自己喜欢某物的委婉方式，像是在承认一点小小的偏好。

abstract.en: A word that means both incomplete and unfair hints that taking a part is already a kind of taking sides.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示「不完整」与「不公平」，暗示「取一部分」本身就是一种「站边」。

abstract.en: Because partial can describe a view, a payment and a referee, the language treats love, money and judgement as the same act of dividing.
abstract.cn: 既然 partial 能形容视野、付款与裁判，语言就把爱、钱与判断都看成同一种「分割」的动作。

abstract.en: The opposite of partial is impartial rather than whole, which suggests that fairness is imagined as owning no share.
abstract.cn: partial 的对立面是 impartial 而不是 whole，这说明「公正」被想象成「不占任何一份」。
