definition_zh: 参与；参加；分享（收益、成本）；持有份额；（古旧）具有某种性质
definition_en: to take part in an activity or share in something with others; in older usage, to have a quality in common with something
core_image: 一只手伸进共同的事务里，并从中分到属于自己的一份
scene: 社区花园里，居民卷起袖子一起翻土、分种子、抬水桶。Everyone who came to the garden was asked to participate, and at the end each helper took home a basket of vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 participate 是「参与活动」（第 1 个义项：参加一项活动）；句意：每个来花园的人都被邀请参与，最后每位帮手都带回家一篮蔬菜。图中可辨识物件：铁锹、种子袋、水桶、菜畦、收成篮；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: （古旧、正式）具有；带有（某种性质）

derivatives.zh: 参与性的（多指管理风格）
不参与的；不参加分红的

senses.title: Take part in an activity
senses.definition: to take part in an event, activity, or process with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起参加某项事件、活动或过程
senses.example: More than fifty students participated in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 五十多名学生参加了这项调查。
senses.why: Latin particeps means 'taking a part', from pars 'part' plus capere 'to take'. To participate is literally to take a part for oneself in something larger, which is why the verb always needs a whole to enter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 particeps 意为“拿取一份”，由 pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”构成。participate 字面就是“在一个更大的事情里为自己拿一份”，因此这个动词总需要一个可进入的整体。

senses.title: Take part actively: put yourself in
senses.definition: to involve oneself actively rather than merely being present
senses.definitionCN: 主动投入，而不只是身在现场
senses.example: She participated eagerly in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她热切地参与了辩论。
senses.why: Taking a part is an action, not a seat. The word therefore implies effort: the participant reaches into the activity, while a spectator only watches it.
senses.whyCN: “拿一份”是动作，不是占个座位。因此这个词隐含付出：参与者把手伸进活动中，而旁观者只是看着。

senses.title: Share in the results
senses.definition: to share in profits, costs, or benefits with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人分享利润、成本或收益
senses.example: The workers participate in the profits of the cooperative.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们分享合作社的利润。
senses.why: The 'part' taken can be a share of the outcome rather than a role in the work. English extends the word from joining an activity to receiving a portion of what the activity produces.
senses.whyCN: 所拿的“一份”可以是成果中的份额，而不只是工作中的一个角色。英语把这个词从“加入活动”扩展到“分得活动产出的一部分”。

senses.title: Hold a share: participating policies
senses.definition: in finance and insurance, to have a right to a share of profits or assets
senses.definitionCN: 在金融与保险中，拥有分得利润或资产的权利
senses.example: The policy is participating, so it receives annual dividends.
senses.exampleCN: 这是分红型保单，因此每年获得红利。
senses.why: Once a share can be owned, participation becomes a property right written into a contract. The word moves from doing to holding, but the underlying image is still a portion set aside for the holder.
senses.whyCN: 当“一份”可以被拥有，参与就变成写进合同的财产权。这个词从“做事”转到“持有”，但底层画面仍是为持有者留出的那一份。

senses.title: Take part in decisions
senses.definition: to have a voice or a role in making decisions that affect a group
senses.definitionCN: 在影响群体的决策中有发言权或一份作用
senses.example: Employees participate in decisions about working hours.
senses.exampleCN: 员工参与有关工时的决策。
senses.why: Decision-making is an activity with roles inside it. To participate is to hold one of those roles, which is why the word appears in arguments about democracy and workplace governance.
senses.whyCN: 决策是一项内部有角色的活动。参与就是持有其中一个角色，因此这个词会出现在关于民主与工作场所治理的讨论中。

senses.title: Enter a competition
senses.definition: to compete or take part in a contest, tournament, or exhibition
senses.definitionCN: 参加比赛、锦标赛或展览
senses.example: Twelve teams participated in the tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 十二支队伍参加了锦标赛。
senses.why: A contest is a structured whole with a fixed number of places. Entering it is taking one of those places, so the verb fits competitions as naturally as meetings.
senses.whyCN: 比赛是一个结构化的整体，名额固定。报名参赛就是占其中一个位置，因此这个动词用于竞赛和用于会议一样自然。

senses.title: Enrol as a research subject
senses.definition: to enrol oneself as a subject in a clinical trial or research study
senses.definitionCN: 作为受试者加入临床试验或研究
senses.example: Two hundred patients participated in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 两百名患者参加了这项试验。
senses.why: In a trial the participant contributes data rather than labour. The word still means taking a part, but the part is now a measured role inside a protocol, and ethics rules grow around it.
senses.whyCN: 在试验中，参与者贡献的是数据而不是劳动。这个词仍表示“拿一份”，但这一份现在是研究方案里被测量的角色，伦理规范也随之围绕它生长。

senses.title: Have a quality in common (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 具有某种性质（古旧用法）
senses.definition: in older usage with of, to have a quality or nature in common with something
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，与 of 连用，表示与某物共有某种性质或本性
senses.example: The essay participates of the nature of a confession.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章带有自白的性质。
senses.why: In scholastic language, sharing a quality was treated as having a share in a form. The construction participate of is a fossil of that metaphysics, which is why it now sounds literary and old.
senses.whyCN: 在经院哲学语言里，“共有一项性质”被理解为“分有一个形式”。participate of 这一结构就是那套形而上学的化石，因此今天听来既文学又古旧。

intro.en: Participate is a Latin verb built from 'part' and 'take'. Its English life began as a back-formation, and the two halves are well documented.
intro.cn: participate 是一个由“部分”与“拿取”构成的拉丁动词。它在英语中的生命始于逆构，两个成分都有明确记载。

items.en: The English verb is recorded, probably a back-formation from participation or taken directly from Latin participatus, the past participle of participare.
items.cn: 英语动词记录于 16 世纪 30 年代，很可能是从 participation 逆构而来，或直接取自拉丁语 participare 的过去分词 participatus。

items.en: Participare 'to share, take part' comes from particeps 'sharing, taking part'. Particeps joins pars 'part' with the -cip- element of capere 'to take, seize'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 participare“分享、参加”来自 particeps“分享的、参加的”。particeps 把 pars“部分”与 capere“拿取、抓住”的 -cip- 成分结合起来。

items.en: Pars goes back to PIE *pere- 'to grant, allot', the family of portion and parcel. Capere goes back to *kap- 'to grasp', the family of capture and accept. The asterisks mark reconstructed roots.
items.cn: pars 上溯原始印欧语 *pere-“给予、分配”，是 portion 与 parcel 的词族。capere 上溯 *kap-“抓取”，是 capture 与 accept 的词族。星号表示重构词根。

items.en: The construction participate of appears, meaning 'to have a quality in common with'. It belongs to scholastic talk of sharing in a form and is now archaic.
items.cn: participate of 这一结构出现于 16 世纪 60 年代，意为“与……共有某种性质”。它属于经院哲学关于“分有形式”的说法，如今已属古旧。

items.en: Finance and insurance extend the word to profit-sharing: participating policy, participating shares. Twentieth-century institutions add participatory democracy and clinical trial participation.
items.cn: 金融与保险把词扩展到利润分享：分红型保单、参与分红的股份。20 世纪的制度又添上“参与式民主”与“临床试验参与”。

note.en: The first group is built on the same part- root but means something else; the second compares verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组同样带 part- 词根但意思不同；第二组比较表示“加入”的动词。

entries.definition: a verb form used as an adjective, such as broken or running. It comes from Latin participium 'a sharing', so it is a relative of participate but not a form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用作形容词的动词形式，如 broken 或 running。它来自拉丁语 participium“分享”，因而是 participate 的亲戚，却不是它的词形变化。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. It is the noun from participate, not a separate verb.
entries.definitionCN: 参与者。它是 participate 派生的名词，不是另一个动词。

entries.definition: the act of taking part. The -ion suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的行为。-ion 后缀把动词变成动作名词。

entries.definition: concerning only a part; biased. It shares the pars root but has no capere element and does not mean taking part.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的；偏袒的。它共享 pars 词根，但没有 capere 成分，也不表示“参加”。

entries.definition: to be present at an event. It stresses presence, while participate stresses contributing or sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 出席某个活动。它强调在场，而 participate 强调贡献或分享。

entries.definition: to become a member of a group or activity. It marks entry, while participate marks the activity once inside.
entries.definitionCN: 成为某群体或活动的一员。它标记“进入”，而 participate 标记进入之后的活动。

entries.definition: to become involved with something, often with commitment. It is broader and can be passive or hostile as well as cooperative.
entries.definitionCN: 投入某事，常含承诺。它更宽泛，既可合作，也可被动甚至对抗。

entries.definition: to give something such as effort, money, or ideas to a shared purpose. It stresses what is given, while participate stresses being one of the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标付出努力、金钱或想法。它强调“给出什么”，而 participate 强调“成为其中一份”。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on part + take, then three abstract images about shares and belonging.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 part + take 的挂钩，再用三个关于“份额与归属”的抽象画面。

normal.en: Split it: parti- is part, -cip- is take (as in capture). Participate = take a part.
normal.cn: 拆开看：parti- 是“部分”，-cip- 是“拿取”（如 capture）。participate＝拿一份。

normal.en: participate in, not participate at: you enter a whole, so the preposition is in.
normal.cn: 是 participate in，不是 participate at：你进入的是一个整体，所以介词用 in。

normal.en: A participant is one who took a part; the -ant ending marks the person holding the share.
normal.cn: participant 就是“拿了那一份的人”；-ant 结尾标记持有这份的人。

normal.en: In a meeting, presence is attendance; speaking is participation. Two different words for two different levels.
normal.cn: 在会上，到场是 attendance，发言才是 participation。两个词对应两个层次。

normal.en: A participating policy pays you a part of the profits; the same 'share' idea, now in money.
normal.cn: 分红型保单（participating policy）把一部分利润分给你；还是“一份”的意思，只是换成了钱。

abstract.en: To participate is to accept a share of both the work and the consequence; the two cannot be separated.
abstract.cn: 参与就是同时接受工作与后果中的一份；这两者无法分开。

abstract.en: A whole is made of parts that agreed to be counted. Participation is the act of being counted.
abstract.cn: 整体由同意被计入的部分组成。参与就是让自己被计入的动作。

abstract.en: The older sense reminds us that things can share a nature, not only a task: participation began as metaphysics before it became management.
abstract.cn: 古旧义提醒我们：事物不仅能共担任务，也能共有本性——参与先是一种形而上学，然后才成为管理术语。

examples.en: All staff are encouraged to participate in the safety review.
examples.cn: 鼓励全体员工参与安全审查。

examples.en: The company participates in a pension scheme for every employee.
examples.cn: 公司为每位员工参加了一项养老金计划。

examples.en: She participated of a stubbornness that ran in the family.
examples.cn: 她身上带有这个家族遗传的固执。

dict_mnemonic.note: parti- 记成“部分”，-cip- 记成“拿”（capere）：伸手拿一份，就是参与。
dict_mnemonic.text: parti（部分）+ cip（拿取）+ -ate（动词）→ 拿一份 → 参与、分享

root: 拉丁 particeps“分享的、参与的”＝pars“部分”（原始印欧语 *pere-“分配”）+ -cip-（capere“拿取”，*kap-）→ participare → participate。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from taking a part in an activity, to taking it actively, to sharing the results, holding a financial share, joining decisions, entering a contest, enrolling in a trial, and finally the old metaphysical sense of sharing a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“在活动中拿一份”开始，转到积极投入、分享成果、持有金融份额、参与决策、报名参赛、加入试验，最后落到古旧的形而上学义：共有一项性质。

core.en: A hand reaching into a shared task and coming away with its own portion
core.cn: 一只手伸进共同的事务，并从中取走属于自己的那一份

chain: HAVE A SHARE OF A QUALITY

branches.en: Entering structured wholes: an activity, a survey, or a tournament with limited places.
branches.cn: 进入结构化的整体：活动、调查，或名额有限的比赛。

branches.en: From effort to voice: active involvement, and a role in deciding.
branches.cn: 从出力到发声：积极投入，以及在决策中的一份角色。

branches.en: The share as income: profit-sharing, and a contractual right to dividends.
branches.cn: 作为收入的份额：分享利润，以及合同上的分红权。

branches.en: The measured role: a trial subject is still taking part, but inside a protocol.
branches.cn: 被测量的角色：受试者仍在“参加”，只是身处研究方案之中。

branches.en: The old sense: to have a quality in common with something, used with of.
branches.cn: 古旧义：与某物共有某种性质，常与 of 连用。

intro.en: Participate belongs to the part- family and the capere family. The derivatives below show the person, the act, the adjective of style, and the financial participle.
intro.cn: participate 属于 part- 词族，也属于 capere 词族。下面的派生词展示了人、行为、风格形容词，以及金融用法中的分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin participare and particeps are the direct sources. Pars gives the 'part', capere gives the 'take'; both are old Latin words with reconstructed PIE roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 participare 与 particeps 是直接来源。pars 提供“部分”，capere 提供“拿取”；两者都是古老拉丁词，有重构的原始印欧语词根。

items.meaning: to take part or share in something

items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都收到一份表格。

items.meaning: organized so that people can take part
items.example: The project uses a participatory method.
items.exampleCN: 该项目采用参与式方法。

items.meaning: allowing or encouraging involvement, especially in management
items.meaningCN: 参与性的，尤指管理风格

items.meaning: not taking part; not sharing in profits
items.exampleCN: 不参与分红的股份没有红利。

items.example: Each part has its own function.
items.exampleCN: 每一部分都有自己的功能。

items.example: The verb captures the idea of taking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词抓住了“拿取”的意思。

items.meaning: taking part; in insurance, sharing in profits

latinEntries.meaning: to share, to take part in
latinEntries.example: Participare is the direct source of English participate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: participare 是英语 participate 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Particeps literally means taking a part.
latinEntries.exampleCN: particeps 字面意为“拿取一份”。

latinEntries.meaning: a part, a portion, a share
latinEntries.example: Pars is the base of portion and partial.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pars 是 portion 与 partial 的基础。
participatio 是英语 participation 的基础。

definition_zh: 粒子；微粒；极少量；语法中的小品词；物理学中的基本粒子
definition_en: an extremely small piece of matter, or a very small unit treated as a physical or grammatical entity
core_image: 阳光斜穿暗室，空气里飘着一粒极小的灰，亮一下又沉下去
scene: 一束阳光斜穿暗室，空气里有一点灰烬在发亮。A single particle of soot drifted across the beam of light.
sceneCN: 这里 particle 指「极小的物质颗粒」（第 1 个义项：肉眼几乎看不见的一小块物质）；句意：一粒烟灰在光柱中缓缓飘过。图中可辨识物件：光柱、悬浮的灰点、暗室、窗缝；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 特定的；讲究的（原义「属于某一小部分的」）
颗粒物（空气污染物指标）

senses.title: A tiny piece of matter
senses.definition: an extremely small piece of solid matter that can be seen only with effort or not at all
senses.definitionCN: 极小的固体物质，肉眼几乎看不见或完全看不见
senses.example: A particle of dust settled on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒灰尘落在镜片上。
senses.why: Latin particula is a diminutive of pars 'part', so the word begins as 'a little part' and keeps that literal smallness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原词是「部分」的指小形式，因此这个词从一开始就是「一小部分」，并保留了这个字面意义。

senses.title: A basic unit in physics
senses.definition: a distinct unit of matter or energy treated as an individual entity, such as an electron or a photon
senses.definitionCN: 被当作独立个体处理的一份物质或能量，如电子或光子
senses.example: The accelerator smashes particles together at nearly the speed of light.
senses.exampleCN: 加速器让粒子以接近光速相互撞击。
senses.why: Physics generalized the little-part idea until it meant the smallest countable unit, whether or not it has mass.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「小部分」推广成「最小可数单元」，无论它是否有质量。

senses.title: A fragment emitted in radiation
senses.titleCN: 放射过程中放出的碎片
senses.definition: a small piece of matter thrown out by a radioactive nucleus, such as an alpha or beta particle
senses.definitionCN: 放射性原子核抛出的微小物质，如阿尔法粒子或贝塔粒子
senses.example: An alpha particle is two protons and two neutrons bound together.
senses.exampleCN: 一个阿尔法粒子就是两个质子与两个中子结合在一起。
senses.why: Early radiation research saw only anonymous specks flying off, so these fragments were simply called particles until they were identified.
senses.whyCN: 早期放射研究只看到无名的小东西飞出，因此在被辨认之前，这些碎片就径称粒子。

senses.title: A short grammatical word
senses.definition: a short word with little meaning of its own that marks a grammatical relation, such as a preposition or a phrasal-verb adverb
senses.definitionCN: 本身意义很弱、用来标记语法关系的短词，如介词或短语动词中的副词
senses.example: The particle 'up' changes the meaning of the verb.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小品词就能改变整个动词的意思。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the word for an uninflected scrap of language that behaves like a loose piece rather than a full word.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借这个词来指不变化的小语言片段，因为它像一块散件，而不像一个完整的词。

senses.title: The word that carries negation
senses.definition: a grammatical element that marks negation, such as 'not' or the negative prefix un-
senses.definitionCN: 标记否定的语法成分，如表示否定的副词或否定前缀
senses.example: In some languages a single particle turns a statement into a denial.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言里，一个小品词就能把陈述变成否认。
senses.why: Negation is often carried by one small fixed word, so the general 'small piece' label settled on it in descriptive grammar.
senses.whyCN: 否定常由一个固定的小词承担，因此描述语法时就把「小片段」这一称呼安在它身上。

senses.title: A minute amount of a quality
senses.titleCN: 某种品质的极微小分量
senses.definition: a very small amount of a quality such as truth, doubt or humour
senses.definitionCN: 真、疑、幽默等品质的极小分量
senses.example: There is not a particle of evidence for the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法没有丝毫证据。
senses.why: The literal speck became a measure of anything that can be divided, so a particle of truth is the smallest imaginable share of it.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的微粒变成衡量可分之物的一把尺，因此「一颗粒子的真相」就是想象中最小的份额。

senses.title: Airborne particulate pollution
senses.definition: one of the fine solid bits suspended in air that are counted as pollution, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮在空气中、被计入污染的细小固体，通常用复数
senses.example: The city measures particles smaller than two and a half microns.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市测量小于两点五微米的颗粒。
senses.why: Air-quality rules needed a countable unit for soot and smoke, and the everyday word for a speck supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 空气质量规则需要给烟尘一个可计数的单位，日常表示微粒的词正好补上。

senses.title: The smallest separable unit of an idea
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：一个想法中最小可分的单位
senses.definition: the smallest piece into which an argument, a story or a system can be divided without losing its identity
senses.definitionCN: 论证、故事或体系在不失去自身特性的前提下能分到的最小单位
senses.example: He rebuilt the theory from its smallest particles of fact.
senses.exampleCN: 他从事实的最小颗粒出发重建了这套理论。
senses.why: The abstract sense treats ideas as matter: anything analysable can be ground down to particles and put back together.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把想法当成物质：凡可分析之物都能磨成颗粒，再重新拼起。

intro.en: Particle comes from Latin particula, a diminutive of pars 'part', through Old French. The smallness is built into the form itself. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: particle 经古法语来自拉丁 particula，而 particula 是「部分」的指小形式。小，是这个词形自带的意思。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pars meant 'part, piece, share'. Its deeper origin is not established beyond the Latin stage.
items.cn: pars 意为「部分、片段、份额」。越过拉丁语阶段之后，它的更早来源没有定论。

items.en: The diminutive suffix made particula 'a little part', a word used for a crumb, a scrap or a small article.
items.cn: 指小后缀造出 particula「一小部分」，用来指碎屑、碎片或小件物品。

items.en: Old French particule carried the word into English, where it first named a small piece of matter or a fragment of a substance.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，最初指一小块物质或某物的一小片。

items.en: By the sixteenth century grammarians had applied it to uninflected function words, giving the sense still used in language teaching.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，语法学家已把它用于不变化的虚词，形成语言教学中仍在使用的义项。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the word named the units revealed by atomic and nuclear research, and particle physics became a discipline.
items.cn: 从十九世纪末起，这个词用来指原子与核研究揭示出的单元，粒子物理学逐渐成为一门学科。

items.en: The first dates for the grammar and physics senses are approximate; the Latin noun itself is fully attested.
items.cn: 语法义与物理义的最早年代为约数；拉丁名词本身有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin part-root or with a similar shape; group two holds size words that overlap with particle in ordinary use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「部分」词根或形状相近的词；第二组是日常使用中与这个词重叠的尺寸词。

entries.definition: From Latin participium, which joins pars 'part' with capere 'to take': a verb form that takes part in two grammatical roles, not a small piece.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁语，把「部分」与「拿取」合起来：指兼有两种语法角色的动词形式，并非小碎片。

entries.definition: Built on the same little-part stock: one specific item singled out, hence detailed or fussy.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「小部分」词源：被单挑出来的某一项，因此引申为具体的、讲究的。

entries.definition: From pars plus -al: only a part of the whole, or favouring one side.
entries.definitionCN: 由「部分」加形容词后缀构成：只是整体的一部分，或偏向一方。

entries.definition: From Latin portio 'share', a relative of pars: an allotted share, usually of something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「份额」，与「部分」同族：指分得的一份，通常属于更大之物。

entries.definition: The smallest unit of a chemical element; it contains many particles and is not itself a fragment.
entries.definitionCN: 化学元素的最小单元；它内部含许多粒子，本身并不是碎片。

entries.definition: Two or more atoms bonded together; it is a structured group rather than a loose speck.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或多个原子结合成的整体；它是有结构的一组，而非松散的一粒。

entries.definition: An ordinary word for a tiny spot or crumb, usually visible; it lacks the technical range of particle.
entries.definitionCN: 日常指可见的小点或碎屑，不含这个粒子词的技术含义。

entries.definition: A small hard piece such as a seed or a grain of sand; it suggests something solid and countable.
entries.definitionCN: 像种子或沙粒那样的小硬块；暗示实体且可数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pars 'part' plus a diminutive suffix: a little part.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「部分」加指小后缀：一小部分。

normal.en: The family runs particle, particulate, particular, partial, portion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括粒子、颗粒状的、特定的、部分的、份额。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical sense: particle physics, particle accelerator, alpha particle.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：粒子物理学、粒子加速器、阿尔法粒子。

normal.en: Grammar uses the same word for little words like up, not and to.
normal.cn: 语法里用同一个词指那些表示方向、否定或连接的小词。

normal.en: Air-quality reports count particles, which is the literal sense applied to pollution.
normal.cn: 空气质量报告清点颗粒物，正是字面义用在污染上。

abstract.en: Picture a single speck held in a sunbeam, the only thing visible in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象光柱里悬着一粒灰，空屋里唯一可见的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence taken apart until only the smallest unchangeable words remain.
abstract.cn: 想象把一句话拆开，直到只剩不可再分的小词。

abstract.en: Picture a proof ground down to its smallest facts and rebuilt from them.
abstract.cn: 想象把一套论证磨成最小的事实颗粒，再由这些颗粒重建。

examples.en: Filters catch particles that the eye cannot see.
examples.cn: 过滤器能截住肉眼看不见的颗粒。

examples.en: Physicists sort particles by mass and charge.
examples.cn: 物理学家按质量与电荷给粒子分类。

examples.en: The report found not a particle of proof.
examples.cn: 报告找不到丝毫证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「part（部分）+ icle（小）」——整体里的一小部分，就是粒子

root: 拉丁 pars「部分」+ 指小后缀 -cula → particula「一小部分」。pars 更早来源不明。英语 particle。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep the literal smallness but change the scale: a speck of dust, a unit of physics, a radiation fragment, a grammar word, a negative marker, a shred of evidence, a pollution count and finally the smallest piece of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留字面上的「小」，只是换了尺度：一粒灰、一个物理单元、一块放射碎片、一个语法小词、一个否定标记、一丝证据、一项污染计数，最后是一个想法的最小碎片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one speck visible in a sunbeam, small enough to be almost nothing yet countable.
core.cn: 核心意象：光柱里可见的一粒灰，小得几乎不存在，却仍能数出来。

branches.en: THE SPECK: dust in a room and soot in the air are the same literal little piece, one domestic and one regulated.
branches.cn: 微粒：屋里的灰与空中的烟尘是同一个字面小片，一个家常，一个受管制。

branches.en: THE UNIT: physics turns the speck into a countable entity, and radiation research turns it into a named fragment.
branches.cn: 单元：物理学把微粒变成可计数实体，放射研究把它变成有名目的碎片。

branches.en: THE SCRAP OF LANGUAGE: an uninflected word is treated as a loose piece, and one such piece can carry negation.
branches.cn: 语言碎片：不变化的词被看作散件，而这样一个散件就能承担否定。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the speck becomes the smallest possible share of a quality such as truth.
branches.cn: 尺度：微粒成为真这类品质的最小可能份额。

branches.en: THE ATOM OF THOUGHT: an argument is ground down to particles and rebuilt.
branches.cn: 思想之原子：一套论证被磨成颗粒，再由颗粒重建。

intro.en: Particle is built from a Latin root for part and a diminutive suffix, and that root also supplies several abstract English words.
intro.cn: particle 由表示「部分」的拉丁词根加指小后缀构成，这个词根还供给若干抽象英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, partis yields part, particle, partial, particular and portion; the diminutive marker is what makes particle mean a small piece rather than a share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「部分」衍生 part、particle、partial、particular 与 portion；指小标记正是让 particle 表示小片而非份额的关键。

items.example: The root states that something is only a piece of a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根说明某物只是整体的一块。

items.example: The suffix shrinks the base noun without changing its kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把基础名词缩小，却不改变它的类别。

items.example: A crumb is a little part of the loaf.
items.exampleCN: 一块碎屑就是面包的一小部分。

items.example: The particle was too small to see.
A partial answer leaves the rest unexplained.
items.exampleCN: 部分回答把其余部分留在未解释中。

items.example: Each particular case needs its own file.
items.exampleCN: 每一个具体个案都需要自己的档案。

items.meaningCN: 以分离颗粒形式存在的
items.example: Particulate matter hangs in the air.
Each heir received a portion of the estate.
items.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得产业的一份。

definition_zh: 特定的；某一个；特别的；讲究的；细节
definition_en: used to point to one specific person or thing rather than any other, special or worth noticing, hard to please about small details, or, as a noun, a single detail of a matter
core_image: 货架前一个人蹲下身，只从一排同样的罐子里挑出标签最正的那一罐
scene: 深夜的茶馆里，一位老客人盯着茶杯，要求换掉这壶已经凉透的茶。She is very particular about the tea she drinks.
sceneCN: 这里的 particular 是「挑剔的、讲究的」（第 3 个义项：对细节要求高）；句意是她对喝的茶十分讲究。图中可辨识物件：茶杯、茶壶、老客人。

pos.zh: 特定的；某一个；特别的；讲究的

derivatives.zh: 由 particular 加 -ly 构成，义为「尤其；特别」
由 particular 加 -ity 构成，义为「特殊性；细处」
由 particular 加 -ize 构成，义为「详述；逐一列举」

senses.title: One specific thing
senses.definition: used to point to one definite person, thing or kind, rather than to any other
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出确定的某个人、物或种类，而不是别的
senses.example: She had a particular reason for choosing that seat.
senses.exampleCN: 她选那个座位有特定的理由。
senses.why: Particular comes from Latin particula, a small part, so the adjective begins by picking out one small item from a larger set.
senses.whyCN: particular 出自拉丁语 particula（小部分），所以这个形容词的起点，是从一大类里挑出小小的一项。

senses.title: Special or worth noticing
senses.definition: greater or more noticeable than usual, so that attention is drawn to it
senses.definitionCN: 比寻常更大或更引人注意，因而把注意力吸引过去
senses.example: This case deserves particular attention.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案例值得特别注意。
senses.why: What has been singled out from the rest is by definition noticeable, so the word for one chosen item drifts into the meaning of special.
senses.whyCN: 既然是从其余之中被单独挑出来的，它按定义就引人注意，于是「被选中的那一个」滑向了「特别的」。

senses.title: Hard to please about details
senses.definition: demanding and careful about small details, especially about food, clothes or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 对细小之处要求严格、十分在意，尤指对食物、衣着或举止
senses.example: She is very particular about the tea she drinks.
senses.exampleCN: 她对喝的茶十分讲究。
senses.why: A person who notices every small part of a thing becomes exacting about parts, so the same word shifts from the item picked out to the person who insists on picking.
senses.whyCN: 一个人若连事物的每个小部分都注意到，就会对「部分」格外苛求；同一个词于是从「被挑出的东西」转指「非要挑的人」。

senses.title: A single detail of a matter
senses.definition: a single fact or detail about something, usually in the plural, as in the particulars of a case
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的某一项事实或细节，通常用复数，如案件的细节
senses.example: The report sets out the particulars of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了协议的细节。
senses.why: When the adjective becomes a noun, the small part it once pointed at stands alone: a particular is one item on a list of details.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词转为名词，它原先指着的那个小部分就独立出来：一条 particular 就是细节清单上的一项。

intro.en: Particular comes from Latin particularis, built on particula, the small form of pars, part; French passed it to English, where it first meant relating to a single item and later also meant fussy about details.
intro.cn: particular 来自拉丁语 particularis，建立在 pars（部分）的小称 particula 之上；经法语进入英语，先指「与单项有关的」，后来又指「对细节挑剔的」。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and nearly every later English word in this family begins there.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，这一族英语词几乎都从这里出发。

items.en: Particula, the small form of pars, named a tiny piece, and its adjective particularis pointed to one such piece.
items.cn: particula 是 pars 的小称，指极小的部分，其形容词 particularis 就指向这样的一小块。

items.en: Particularis described what belongs to a single item rather than to the whole class.
items.cn: particularis 描述属于某一个单项、而非整个类别的东西。

items.en: Old French kept the word as particulier, meaning individual or specific, and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 particulier，意为个别的、特定的，并把它传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the sense of one specific item, adds the sense of special attention, and develops the noun particulars for details.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「特定的一项」，加上「格外注意」的意思，又发展出名词 particulars 表示细节。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the whole part family in view, so particular is not confused with partial or partly; the near-meaning group gathers words for one exact item, for fussiness and for details.
note.cn: 形近组把整个 part 一族摆在一起，避免把 particular 与 partial、partly 弄混；近义组收表示「特定的某一项」「挑剔」与「细节」的词。

entries.definition: Very or especially, used to single something out for emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 非常、尤其，用来把某事单独拎出来强调。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: Covering only a part, or favouring one side.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的，或偏袒一方的。

entries.definition: A wrapped package or a plot of land, from the same small Latin piece.
entries.definitionCN: 包裹或一块地，出自同一个拉丁语「小块」。

entries.definition: Clearly defined and exact, not general.
entries.definitionCN: 明确具体的，而非笼统的。

entries.definition: Different from what is usual and worth attention.
entries.definitionCN: 与寻常不同、值得注意的。

entries.definition: Hard to please, especially about small details.
entries.definitionCN: 难以取悦的，尤指对细节挑剔。

entries.definition: A single small fact or feature of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事中的一项细小事实或特征。

normalIntro.en: Particular points at one small piece picked out of a set, and its hooks follow that piece into special notice, into fussiness and finally into a written item.
normalIntro.cn: particular 指向从一类中挑出的那一小块，记忆钩子顺着这一小块，走到「格外注意」，再走到「挑剔」，最后落到纸面上的一项。

normal.en: Particular and partial both come from Latin pars, but particular picks one item out, while partial describes only a part of it.
normal.cn: particular 与 partial 都出自拉丁语 pars，但 particular 是挑出某一项，partial 则是只占某物的一部分。

normal.en: In particular singles out one case from many, which is exactly what the adjective does on its own.
normal.cn: in particular 从许多当中单独拎出一例，这正是这个形容词本身的动作。

normal.en: Particular about keeps the same act of picking: a fussy person inspects every small part before choosing.
normal.cn: particular about 保留了同一个「挑」的动作：挑剔的人在选之前把每个小处都看一遍。

normal.en: As a noun, particulars are the separate items of a case, each one a small part written down.
normal.cn: 作名词时，particulars 是一件事的各个单项，每一条都是记下来的一个小部分。

normal.en: Particularly is the adverb and usually means especially, not in a partial way.
normal.cn: particularly 是副词，通常意为「尤其」，而不是「以部分的方式」。

abstract.en: A word that can mean both specific and fussy suggests that attention to detail and being hard to please are one habit seen from two sides.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能表示「特定的」又能表示「挑剔的」，说明关注细节与难以取悦是同一个习惯的两面。

abstract.en: To call something particular is to say it has been separated from its class, and separation is the first step toward value.
abstract.cn: 把某物称作 particular，就是说它已从同类中分离出来，而分离正是价值的第一步。

abstract.en: The noun particulars turns attention into a list, which is how a habit of noticing becomes a document.
abstract.cn: 名词 particulars 把注意力变成一张清单，注意到细节的习惯就这样成了一份文件。

examples.en: She had a particular reason for choosing that seat.
examples.cn: 她选那个座位有特定的理由。

examples.en: She is very particular about the tea she drinks.
examples.cn: 她对喝的茶十分讲究。

examples.en: The report sets out the particulars of the agreement.
examples.cn: 报告列出了协议的细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕剔」——挑水果的人怕剔得不干净，一个个翻看；记住 particular 是「特定的」，也是「挑剔的」。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）经小称 particula 派生 particularis（属于单项的），再经古法语 particulier 进入英语；与 partial、partly、particle 同出 part，但 particular 走的是「挑出单项—格外注意—对细节挑剔」这一路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one small piece picked out of a set; the senses divide into the specific item, the special notice it draws, the fussiness of a careful chooser, and the written detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从一类中挑出的那一小块；义项按「特定的那一项」「因此得到的格外注意」「挑剔者的苛求」「落到纸面的细节」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stooping before a shelf to pick the one jar whose label sits perfectly straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架前一个人蹲下身，只从一排同样的罐子里挑出标签最正的那一罐。

branches.en: a single seat chosen for a private reason
branches.cn: 因私人理由选定的一个座位

branches.en: one jar taken from a row of identical jars
branches.cn: 从一排同样的罐子里取出的一罐

branches.en: a footnote that asks for closer reading
branches.cn: 要求读者细看的一条脚注

branches.en: a host who tastes the tea before serving it
branches.cn: 上茶前先尝一口的主人

branches.en: a contract read out item by item
branches.cn: 逐条念出的合同

intro.en: Latin pars and its small form particula sit under a Latin adjective, French reshapes it, and English adds three endings for the adverb, the noun of quality and the verb.
intro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 及其小称 particula 托起一个拉丁形容词，法语改变了它的形状，英语再加三个词缀，造出副词、表性质的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, particula and particularis are all recorded, so this word has a documented Latin ancestry shared with partial, partly and parcel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars、particula 与 particularis 均有记录，因此这个词有据可查的拉丁世系，并与 partial、partly、parcel 同源。

definition_zh: 尤其；特别；格外
definition_en: especially, or in a way that singles out one part of a larger whole
core_image: 一排相同的灯泡里，有一盏被单独调亮
scene: 评审意见先谈整体，再把问题指向其中一处细节。The review praised the design, particularly the door handles.
sceneCN: 这里指从整体中单举一项（第 2 个义项：具体到某一项）；句意是评论称赞了设计，尤其是门把手；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Especially in degree
senses.definition: more than usual or more than others in degree
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上超过平常或超过其他
senses.example: The winter was particularly harsh in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的冬天格外严酷。
senses.why: Modifying an adjective, it raises the degree and invites a comparison with other times or places.
senses.whyCN: 修饰形容词时，它抬高程度，并引出与其他时间或地点的比较。

senses.title: In particular
senses.definition: used to single out one part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 用来从较大的整体中单举一部分
senses.example: The report discusses costs, particularly labour costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告讨论了成本，尤其是人力成本。
senses.why: Here the word narrows a general category to one member, close to specifically.
senses.whyCN: 这里它把一般类别收窄到某一成员，接近「具体地」。

senses.title: Sentence-opening emphasis
senses.definition: placed first to announce the most striking fact
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，宣布最引人注目的事实
senses.example: Particularly striking was the silence in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 特别引人注目的是大厅里的沉默。
senses.why: The front position turns the highlighted element into the sentence's point of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把被强调的成分变成整句的落点。

senses.title: Not particularly
senses.definition: used with not to lower a quality in a polite understatement
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，礼貌地压低某种性质
senses.example: I am not particularly interested in that offer.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那个提议不太感兴趣。
senses.why: The negated form means less than very, a soft refusal rather than a plain no.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式意为「不到很的程度」，是柔和拒绝，而不是直截了当的「不」。

senses.title: Especially given
senses.definition: used before a phrase that strengthens the reasons for a statement
senses.definitionCN: 放在强化理由的短语前
senses.example: The schedule is tight, particularly given the staff shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 日程很紧，尤其考虑到人手不足。
senses.why: The construction adds a factor that makes the claim more forceful, often in argument.
senses.whyCN: 这一结构补上一个使说法更有力的因素，常用于论证。

senses.title: Particularly where or when
senses.definition: used before a clause to mark the case in which a statement matters most
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句前，标出该说法最适用的情形
senses.example: The rule matters particularly when records are shared.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则在记录被共享时尤其重要。
senses.why: The clause restricts the emphasis to a specific circumstance instead of the whole topic.
senses.whyCN: 从句把强调限制在特定情形上，而不是整个话题。

senses.title: Particularly + noun group
senses.definition: used to single out a group affected by a general statement
senses.definitionCN: 用来单举受一般性说法影响的某一群体
senses.example: The change will affect staff, particularly those near retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 这一改动会影响员工，尤其是临近退休的人。
senses.why: The pattern picks out the subset that carries the main burden.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式挑出承担主要影响的那一子集。

senses.title: Formal written emphasis
senses.definition: in formal prose, a more precise alternative to especially
senses.definitionCN: 在正式散文中，作为「尤其」更精确的替代
senses.example: The findings are particularly relevant to small clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这些发现对小诊所尤其相关。
senses.why: Formal writing prefers the word when the emphasis is on a specific case rather than a general high degree.
senses.whyCN: 当强调落在具体情形而非一般的「很」时，正式文字更偏爱这个词。

intro.en: Particularly comes from the Latin word for a small part, through its adjective and French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「小部分」一词，经形容词与法语，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun pars, stem part-, means a part or share.
items.cn: 名词词干意为「部分、份额」。

items.en: The diminutive particula means a small part or particle.
items.cn: 指小形式意为「小部分、微粒」。

items.en: The adjective particularis means belonging to a single part or case.
items.cn: 形容词意为「属于某一部分或个别情形的」。

items.en: English particular passes through French and means specific rather than general.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，意为「特定的」而非「一般的」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage separates precise singling out from mere intensity, especially in formal prose.
items.cn: 现代用法把「精确单举」与「单纯加强」分开，正式散文尤其如此。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin small-part stem; the second group contrasts precise singling out with broader degree intensifiers.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「小部分」词干；第二组对照「精确单举」与更宽泛的程度加强词。

entries.definition: Specific rather than general; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 特定而非一般的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The quality of being specific or detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 特定或详尽的性质。

entries.definition: To state something item by item.
entries.definitionCN: 逐项说明某事。

entries.definition: A very small piece; the same diminutive stem without the adjective ending.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的碎片；同一指小词干，未加形容词词尾。

entries.definition: Above all, or to a high degree; broader because it can simply intensify.
entries.definitionCN: 首先、格外；更宽，因为它可以单纯加强程度。

entries.definition: In a precise and identified way, without the degree sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以精确、指明的方式，不含程度义。

entries.definition: In a way worth noticing; often highlights an example or visible degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以值得注意的方式；常突出例子或可见程度。

entries.definition: The phrase form that singles out one member of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 单举群体中某一成员的短语形式。

entries.definition: More than everything else, ranking first in importance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，在重要性上排第一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real small-part stem and the real split between precision and intensity.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「小部分」词干，并区分「精确」与「强度」。

normal.en: The root is a small part, so the word pulls one piece out of the whole.
normal.cn: 词根是「小部分」，所以它从整体里拉出一块。

normal.en: The report discusses costs, particularly labour costs: that is the word doing its precise work.
normal.cn: 「报告讨论成本，尤其是人力成本」正是这个词在精确单举。

normal.en: Not particularly is a polite way to say not very, not a flat no.
normal.cn: 「不太」是礼貌地说「不是很」，而不是硬邦邦的拒绝。

normal.en: Particularly given adds a reason that makes the claim heavier.
normal.cn: 「尤其考虑到」补上一个让说法更重的理由。

normal.en: In formal prose it often replaces especially when the point is a specific case.
normal.cn: 正式文字里，当重点是具体情形时，它常替代「尤其」。

abstract.en: To be particular is to refuse the comfort of a general statement.
abstract.cn: 「具体」就是拒绝一般性说法带来的舒适。

abstract.en: A bright single lamp changes a row of identical lamps into a picture with a subject.
abstract.cn: 一盏单独调亮的灯，把一排相同的灯变成有主体的画面。

abstract.en: Precision and intensity are different tools, and the word can be either one.
abstract.cn: 精确与强度是两种不同的工具，而这个词两样都能当。

examples.en: The north is particularly cold in January.
examples.cn: 北方在一月格外寒冷。

examples.en: I am not particularly fond of crowded trains.
examples.cn: 我不太喜欢拥挤的火车。

examples.en: The rule was written particularly for small firms.
examples.cn: 这条规则尤其是为小公司写的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「怕提扣了利」——特别怕漏掉某一项，所以单独点出来

root: 拉丁语名词「部分」加指小后缀成「小部分」，再构成形容词「属于个别情形的」；英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate degree emphasis, precise singling out, sentence-opening emphasis, negated understatement, added reasons, restricted circumstances, singled-out groups and formal written emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理程度加强、精确单举、句首强调、否定式低调、补充理由、限定情形、单举群体，以及正式书面强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp in a row turned brighter than all the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排相同的灯泡里，有一盏被单独调亮。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: more than usual or more than others.
branches.cn: 程度：超过平常或超过其他。

branches.en: THE SINGLED ITEM: one part of a whole, and one affected group.
branches.cn: 单举项：整体中的一部分，以及受影响的某一群体。

branches.en: THE FRONT POSITION: emphasis placed at the head of the sentence.
branches.cn: 前置位置：放在句首的强调。

branches.en: THE SOFT OR STRENGTHENED CLAIM: not particularly lowers, particularly given raises.
branches.cn: 柔化或加强的说法：「不太」压低，「尤其考虑到」抬高。

branches.en: THE RESTRICTED CASE: a circumstance clause and the formal register of precision.
branches.cn: 受限情形：限定情形的从句，以及精确的正式语域。

intro.en: Particularly is a Latin part-noun, a diminutive suffix, an adjective suffix, a French layer and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「部分」名词、指小后缀、形容词后缀、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for a part builds a diminutive for a small part, then an adjective for what belongs to one case.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「部分」的名词先构成「小部分」的指小形式，再构成「属于个别情形」的形容词。

items.example: The noun is the general idea of a piece of a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是「整体中的一块」这一总概念。

items.example: The suffix shrinks a part into a small piece.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「部分」缩成小块。

items.example: The small part is the base of the adjective.
The suffix turns the small part into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「小部分」变成表归属的形容词。

items.example: The adjective separates one case from the general class.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把个别情形从一般类别中分出。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for a precise case.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词指精确的个别情形。

items.example: The noun names the quality of being specific.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名「具体」这一性质。

items.example: The verb turns precision into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「精确」变成动作。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into an emphasis adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成强调副词。

definition_zh: 部分地；不完全地；部分因为
definition_en: to some degree but not completely, or used before a reason to say that it is only one of several causes
core_image: 一张桌子一半刷成白色，另一半还留着原来的木色
scene: 午后的天空一半蓝一半灰，云层压得很低。The sky was partly covered by grey clouds.
sceneCN: 这里的 partly 是「部分地、不完全地」（第 1 个义项：只涉及整体的一部分）；句意为天空有一部分被灰云遮住。图中可辨识物件：灰云、露出一角的蓝天、低垂的云层。

pos.zh: 部分地；不完全地；部分因为

derivatives.zh: partly 所由构成的词，义为「部分；角色」
由 part 加 -ial 构成，义为「部分的；偏袒的」
由拉丁词干 part- 加 -ition 构成，义为「分隔；隔断」

senses.title: To some degree, not completely
senses.definition: in some measure or to some degree, but not entirely
senses.definitionCN: 在某种程度上，但不是全部
senses.example: The sky was partly covered by grey clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 天空有一部分被灰云遮住。
senses.why: Partly is part plus the old English adverb ending -ly, so it names the share a thing takes without claiming the whole.
senses.whyCN: partly 是 part 加上古英语副词词尾 -ly，所以它只说一件事占了其中一份，并不声称占了全部。

senses.title: One of several causes
senses.definition: used before a reason to show that it is only one of the causes of something
senses.definitionCN: 用在原因之前，表示它只是造成某事的若干原因之一
senses.example: She left the city partly because of the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开这座城市，部分是因为噪音。
senses.why: When a whole result has several sources, each source supplies only a part, so the adverb naturally introduces one reason among others.
senses.whyCN: 当一个结果有多个来源，每个来源只提供其中一份，于是这个副词很自然地引出诸多原因中的一个。

senses.title: To a limited degree
senses.definition: used with adjectives to limit how strongly a quality is claimed, as opposed to wholly or entirely
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词连用，限定某种性质被肯定的程度，与 wholly、entirely 相对
senses.example: His explanation was partly right and partly wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释对了一半，也错了一半。
senses.why: The same share logic applies to qualities: if only a part of something fits a description, the adjective can only be granted in part.
senses.whyCN: 同一套「份额」逻辑也适用于性质：如果某物只有一部分符合某种描述，那么这个形容词也只能被部分地承认。

intro.en: Partly is an English formation from the noun part and the old adverb ending -ly, and part itself reached English from Latin pars through French.
intro.cn: partly 是英语用名词 part 加古副词词尾 -ly 构成，而 part 本身经法语从拉丁语 pars 传入英语。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and it is the source of part, partial, particular and parcel alike.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，是 part、partial、particular、parcel 共同的来源。

items.en: Old French part kept the sense of a share or a portion and gave the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 part 保留「一份、一部分」的意思，并把词传给英语。

items.en: The English adverb ending -lice, later -ly, turned nouns and adjectives into adverbs of manner.
items.cn: 古英语副词词尾 -lice（后来写作 -ly）把名词与形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Middle English joined part and -ly to make partly, an adverb for something done or true in part.
items.cn: 中古英语把 part 与 -ly 合成 partly，用来表示某事只在部分上成立。

items.en: Modern English uses partly for incomplete states and for one cause among several, and pairs it with wholly and entirely.
items.cn: 现代英语用 partly 表示不完全的状态与诸多原因之一，并让它与 wholly、entirely 相对。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the part family and the two adjective forms that learners often mix with this adverb; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of saying in part.
note.cn: 形近组展示 part 一族，以及学习者常与这个副词混淆的两个形容词；近义组收其他表示「部分地」的说法。

entries.definition: A piece of a whole, or a role in a play.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分，或戏剧中的角色。

entries.definition: Covering only a part, or favouring one side.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的，或偏袒一方的。

entries.definition: One specific item rather than any other.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的某一项，而不是别的。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒。

entries.definition: In part, often used in formal or technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 部分地，多用于正式或技术性文字。

entries.definition: A little, to a limited degree.
entries.definitionCN: 有点儿，在有限程度上。

entries.definition: Partly, when a whole is being divided among causes.
entries.definitionCN: 部分地，用于把整体分给若干原因时。

entries.definition: To the extent of one of two equal parts.
entries.definitionCN: 达到两个相等部分之一的程度。

normalIntro.en: Partly is the plainest form of the part family: it adds an adverb ending to the noun and keeps only the idea of a share.
normalIntro.cn: partly 是 part 一族里最朴素的形式：给名词加一个副词词尾，只保留「占一份」的意思。

normal.en: Partly is part plus -ly, and the ending changes a share into the manner of being true only in part.
normal.cn: partly 是 part 加 -ly，这个结尾把「一份」变成了「只在部分上成立」的方式。

normal.en: Partial is the adjective and partially the longer adverb, while partly is the short everyday choice.
normal.cn: partial 是形容词，partially 是较长的副词，partly 则是日常里更短的选择。

normal.en: Partly usually limits a state or a cause, as in partly cloudy or partly because of the rain.
normal.cn: partly 通常限定一种状态或一个原因，如 partly cloudy 或 partly because of the rain。

normal.en: Particular looks similar but points to one specific item, so the two words must not be swapped.
normal.cn: particular 看起来相近，却指向特定的某一项，两个词不能互换。

normal.en: Because partly already means not wholly, pairing it with completely creates a contradiction.
normal.cn: 既然 partly 本来就表示「不全是」，再与 completely 连用就自相矛盾。

abstract.en: An adverb that only ever claims a share is a lesson in modesty: it leaves room for the rest of the truth.
abstract.cn: 一个始终只声称占一份的副词，是一堂关于克制的课：它给其余的真相留了位置。

abstract.en: Partly because turns a single cause into one thread among several, which is how most real explanations work.
abstract.cn: partly because 把单一原因变成若干线索中的一条，现实中的解释大多如此。

abstract.en: The same word can colour weather, blame and belief, because every judgement covers only part of what is there.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能修饰天气、责任与看法，因为我们所作的每个判断，都只覆盖了存在之物的一部分。

examples.en: The sky was partly covered by grey clouds.
examples.cn: 天空有一部分被灰云遮住。

examples.en: She left the city partly because of the noise.
examples.cn: 她离开这座城市，部分是因为噪音。

examples.en: His explanation was partly right and partly wrong.
examples.cn: 他的解释对了一半，也错了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕脱离」——一队人里只有一部分人怕脱离队伍；记住 partly 是「部分地、不完全地」。

root: 由英语 part（部分，经法语上溯拉丁语 pars）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；与 partial、particular、parcel 同出 part，但 partly 只表示「占其中一部分」，不涉及偏袒或特定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a share of a whole; the senses divide into an incomplete state, one cause among several, and a limited degree of a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是整体中的一份；义项按「不完全的状态」「诸多原因之一」「性质被限定的程度」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table painted white on one half, the other half still bare wood.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子一半刷成白色，另一半还留着原来的木色。

branches.en: a sky half blue and half grey
branches.cn: 一半蓝一半灰的天空

branches.en: a wall painted up to the middle
branches.cn: 只刷到一半的一面墙

branches.en: a family moving away for the noise
branches.cn: 因噪音而搬走的一家人

branches.en: a price rise blamed on several causes
branches.cn: 被归因于多个原因的涨价

branches.en: an answer that is right in places
branches.cn: 只在某些地方正确的回答

intro.en: The word joins an old noun for a share with the English adverb ending, and the noun itself came from Latin through French.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示「一份」的古老名词与英语副词词尾接在一起，而那个名词本身经法语来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars is recorded, and part reached English through French, so partly has the same documented Latin ancestry as partial and particular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 有记录，part 经法语进入英语，因此 partly 与 partial、particular 有同样有据可查的拉丁世系。

definition_zh: 伙伴；搭档；合伙人；配偶；与……合伙
definition_en: a person who shares an activity, a business, or a life with another; also to join with someone as a partner
core_image: 两个人各执一端，抬着同一件重物往前走
scene: 双人皮划艇上，前后两人各握一支桨。The two paddlers must keep exactly the same rhythm, because each one is the partner of the other and the boat goes straight only when they pull together.
sceneCN: 这里 partner 是「搭档」（第 2 个义项：并肩干活的搭档）；句意：两名划手必须保持完全一致的节奏，因为彼此是对方的搭档，只有同时划桨船才会走直。图中可辨识物件：双人皮划艇、两支桨、救生衣、水面、同步的桨痕；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 合伙关系；伙伴关系；合伙企业
已有伴侣的；结成搭档的

senses.title: One who shares a business
senses.titleCN: 共同经营一份生意的人
senses.definition: a person who shares the ownership and risks of a business with one or more others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人共同拥有一家企业并分担风险的人
senses.example: She became a partner in the firm last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年成了这家事务所的合伙人。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'one who shares'. In business the shared thing is ownership itself, so a partner is someone who holds a portion of the firm and is liable for its debts.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是“分享者”。在商业中，被分享的东西就是所有权本身，因此合伙人就是持有企业一份、并对债务负责的人。

senses.title: The one you work beside
senses.definition: a person who works with you on a task, often as an equal
senses.definitionCN: 与你共同完成一项任务的人，通常是平等的一方
senses.example: My lab partner and I split the experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 我和实验搭档分担了实验。
senses.why: Sharing can be sharing work rather than property. Two people each take one end of the task, and equality is built into the word: a partner is not a helper but a counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 分享的对象可以是工作而不是财产。两人各执任务的一端，平等就写在这个词里：partner 不是帮手，而是对等的一方。

senses.title: The one you share a life with
senses.definition: a spouse or a person with whom one lives in a committed romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 配偶，或与之处于稳定恋爱关系并共同生活的人
senses.example: He brought his partner to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他带伴侣来参加晚宴。
senses.why: A life is the largest thing two people can share. English extended partner to the domestic sphere in the 18th century, and the word now avoids the assumptions built into husband or wife.
senses.whyCN: 生活是两个人能分享的最大一件事。英语在 18 世纪把 partner 扩展到家庭领域，如今这个词也避开了 husband 或 wife 所带的预设。

senses.title: The one across the table or on the floor
senses.titleCN: 桌对面或舞池里的搭档
senses.definition: the person matched with you in a game, dance, or performance
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏、舞蹈或表演中与你配对的人
senses.example: She danced with a new partner at the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中与一位新舞伴跳舞。
senses.why: A dance or a game assigns roles that only work in pairs. The partner is the other half of a required pair, which is why the word appears wherever a form demands two.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈或游戏分配的角色只有成对才成立。partner 是某个必需配对中的另一半，因此凡是形式要求两人时，这个词就会出现。

senses.title: Partner in crime: the other half of a secret
senses.definition: a person who joins another in a mischievous or criminal activity, often used humorously
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起干顽皮或犯罪之事的人，常作幽默用法
senses.example: The two children were partners in crime all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个孩子整个夏天都是“共犯”。
senses.why: The phrase borrows the equality of partnership for something illegal. What is shared is not property but risk and secrecy, and the humorous use keeps the bond while dropping the crime.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把伙伴关系的“平等”借给了非法之事。被分享的不是财产，而是风险与秘密；幽默用法保留了这份联结，却抽掉了犯罪。

senses.title: A partner organisation or country
senses.definition: an organisation, company, or country that cooperates formally with another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方正式合作的机构、公司或国家
senses.example: The university is a partner in the research consortium.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学是该研究联盟的合作方。
senses.why: Institutions also pair up. Here partnership is a formal relation between entities rather than between persons, but the logic is the same: each brings something and both are bound.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会结对。这里的伙伴关系是实体之间而非人与人之间的正式关系，但逻辑相同：各方都拿出东西，也都受约束。

senses.title: To partner: join as an equal
senses.titleCN: 动词：作为平等一方加入
senses.definition: to join with someone or an organisation as a partner
senses.definitionCN: 作为伙伴与某人或某机构结合
senses.example: The startup partnered with a larger manufacturer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司与一家更大的制造商结成了伙伴。
senses.why: The verb turns the relation into an act. Partnering is not hiring or assisting; it is the moment two parties agree to stand on the same level, which is why it is popular in business language.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个关系变成动作。partnering 不是雇佣也不是帮忙，而是两方同意站在同一高度的那一刻，因此它在商业语言里很受欢迎。

senses.title: A partner in a professional firm
senses.definition: a senior member of a law or accounting firm who shares in its ownership and profits
senses.definitionCN: 律师事务所或会计师事务所中持有所有权并分享利润的高级成员
senses.example: Only partners may sign the audit report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有合伙人才能签署审计报告。
senses.why: Professional firms are owned by their senior members, so 'partner' becomes a rank as well as a relation. The title marks both ownership and the right to sign, which is why it is a career goal in law and accounting.
senses.whyCN: 专业事务所由其高级成员拥有，因此 partner 既是关系也是职级。这个头衔同时标记所有权与签署权，所以它成了法律与会计行业的一个职业目标。

intro.en: Partner began as a word for a joint heir and was reshaped by the unrelated word part. The deeper root is Latin pars, but the change from parcener to partner is not fully explained.
intro.cn: partner 最初指共同继承人，后来被另一个词 part 改形。更深词根是拉丁语 pars，但从 parcener 变成 partner 的过程并没有完整解释。

items.en: Partiner is recorded meaning 'partner, sharer'. It is an altered form of parcener 'joint heir, one who shares an inheritance'.
items.cn: partiner 记录于 1300 年前后，意为“伙伴、分享者”。它是 parcener“共同继承人、分得遗产者”的变形。

items.en: Parcener comes from Old French parçonier, from parçon 'division, share', from Latin partitionem 'a dividing', from partire 'to divide', from pars 'part'.
items.cn: parcener 来自古法语 parçonier，再上溯 parçon“分割、一份”，拉丁语 partitionem“划分”，动词 partire“分割”，以及 pars“部分”。

items.en: The -n- of parcener becomes -t-, giving partner. The change is usually attributed to the influence of part, though the exact path is source uncertain.
items.cn: parcener 中的 -n- 变成 -t-，形成 partner。这一变化通常归因于 part 的影响，但确切过程来源不确定。

items.en: The commercial sense 'one who shares in a business' is recorded. The legal and commercial senses grow together, since a partnership is both a relation and a form of ownership.
items.cn: “共同经营生意者”这一商业义记录于 16 世纪 20 年代。法律义与商业义一起成长，因为合伙既是一种关系，也是一种所有权形式。

items.en: The sense 'spouse' is recorded. Modern English extends it to any committed couple and to institutional cooperation: trading partner, partner with.
items.cn: “配偶”义记录于 1749 年。现代英语把它扩展到任何稳定的伴侣关系，也扩展到机构合作：贸易伙伴、与……合作。

note.en: The first group shares the part- root or the -er ending; the second compares words for people joined by work, trust, or love.
note.cn: 第一组共享 part- 词根或 -er 结尾；第二组比较因工作、信任或爱情而结合的人。

entries.definition: concerning only a part; biased in favour of one side. It is an adjective, not a person, and has nothing to do with partnership.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的；偏袒一方的。它是形容词，不指人，也与合伙无关。

entries.definition: a division into parts, or a screen that divides a space. It shares the Latin pars root but names a dividing, not a sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 分成若干部分，或隔开空间的屏风。它共享拉丁语 pars 词根，但命名的是“分开”，不是“分享”。

entries.definition: a strong supporter of a party or cause. Its part is a political side, not a share held with another person.
entries.definitionCN: 某一党派或事业的坚定支持者。它的 part 指政治一方，而不是与他人共持的一份。

entries.definition: a very small piece of matter. It is a small part, with the diminutive -cle, and is not a partner.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒。它是“小部分”，带指小后缀 -cle，不是伙伴。

entries.definition: a person you work with, especially in a profession. It is neutral about equality and ownership, while partner implies a share.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共事的人，尤指同一专业。它对平等与所有权保持中性，而 partner 隐含“持有一份”。

entries.definition: a state or person joined with another for mutual support. It is about interests and conflict, while partner can be about work or life.
entries.definitionCN: 为相互支持而结合的国家或个人。它关乎利益与冲突，而 partner 可以关乎工作或生活。

entries.definition: a person who spends time with you. It stresses company, while partner stresses a shared role or share.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共度时光的人。它强调陪伴，而 partner 强调共同的角色或份额。

entries.definition: a husband or wife in law. It is the legal term, while partner is broader and can name an unmarried couple.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上的丈夫或妻子。它是法律术语，而 partner 更宽泛，也可指未婚伴侣。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sound and the shared load, then three abstract images about equality.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕读音与“共抬一物”的挂钩，再用三个关于“平等”的抽象画面。

normal.en: partner has part inside it: a partner holds a part. The spelling hides the old parcener, but the meaning kept the share.
normal.cn: partner 里面藏着 part：partner 持有一份。拼写掩盖了古老的 parcener，但词义保住了“份额”。

normal.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy box, one at each end. Neither is the boss.
normal.cn: 想两个人抬一个重箱子，各执一端。谁都不是老板。

normal.en: Business partner, dance partner, life partner: the same word slides from money to floor to home.
normal.cn: 商业合伙人、舞伴、人生伴侣：同一个词从钱滑到舞池，再滑到家。

normal.en: partner with, not partner to: the preposition marks standing alongside, not belonging to.
normal.cn: 是 partner with，不是 partner to：介词标记“并肩”，不是“附属”。

normal.en: A law firm promotes you to partner: the title means you now own a piece of the firm.
normal.cn: 律师事务所把你提升为 partner：这个头衔意味着你现在拥有事务所的一份。

abstract.en: A partner is equality made practical: two people who each hold one end and cannot move without the other.
abstract.cn: 伙伴是被实践出来的平等：两人各执一端，缺少对方就无法前进。

abstract.en: Partnership is a share in risk before it is a share in reward; that is why the word fits both marriage and business.
abstract.cn: 合伙先是风险中的一份，然后才是收益中的一份；因此这个词同时适用于婚姻与商业。

abstract.en: Calling someone a partner rather than a helper is a claim about dignity, not about workload.
abstract.cn: 称一个人为 partner 而不是 helper，是在主张尊严，而不是分配工作量。

examples.en: The two firms became partners in a joint venture.
examples.cn: 这两家公司在一次合资中成为合伙人。

examples.en: He partnered with a local charity to rebuild the school.
examples.cn: 他与当地一家慈善机构合作重建了学校。

examples.en: Her partner stayed home while she attended the conference.
examples.cn: 她去开会时，伴侣留在了家里。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 part 记成“一份”，-ner 记成人：持有一份的人，就是合伙人、搭档、伴侣。
dict_mnemonic.text: part（一份）+ -ner（人）→ 持有一份的人 → 合伙人、搭档、伴侣

root: 古法语 parçonier < parçon“分割、一份” < 拉丁 partitionem / partire < pars“部分”；拼写受 part 影响，由 parcener 变为 partner。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from shared ownership, to shared work, to a shared life, to a required pair in a game or dance, to a shared secret, to institutional cooperation, to the act of joining, and finally to the rank inside a professional firm.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从共同所有权，转到共担工作、共同生活、游戏或舞蹈中必需的另一半、共同保守的秘密、机构合作、结伴的动作，最后落到专业事务所内部的职级。

core.en: Two people holding one end each of the same load, walking in step
core.cn: 两人各执同一重物的一端，步调一致地前行

branches.en: Ownership: a share in a firm, and the rank that share confers.
branches.cn: 所有权：在企业中的一份，以及这份所有权带来的职级。

branches.en: The required other half: a workmate on a task, and a mate in a dance or game.

definition_en: a business or working relationship between partners, or the state of being partners in an activity

sceneCN: 这里 partnership 指「两个主体共同出资、共同承担的合作关系」（第 1 个义项：商业上的合伙）；句意为两家公司组成合伙关系，以投标这项桥梁工程。可辨识物件：木牌、两个姓氏、投标文件、模型桥；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 合伙；合伙企业；伙伴关系

senses.title: A firm owned by partners
senses.definition: a business in which two or more people share ownership, profits and liability
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或更多人共同拥有、共享利润并共担责任的企业
senses.example: The two firms formed a partnership to bid for the bridge contract.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司组成合伙关系，以投标这项桥梁工程。
senses.why: the noun ending -ship marks a state or a body, so partner plus -ship can name the firm itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾 -ship 标记一种状态或一个团体，因此 partner 加 -ship 可以直接命名这家企业。

senses.title: The relationship of partners
senses.definition: the working relation between people who share an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 共同经营一项事业的人之间的工作关系
senses.example: Their partnership survived two failed ventures.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的合伙关系在两次失败的项目之后仍然存续。
senses.why: the same ending can name the bond rather than the body, which is why the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾既可以命名「关系」，也可以命名「团体」，因此这个词同时覆盖两者。

senses.title: Cooperation between organizations
senses.definition: a formal working arrangement between bodies that remain separate
senses.definitionCN: 各自独立的两方之间正式的工作安排
senses.example: The city entered a partnership with the railway company.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府与铁路公司建立了合作关系。
senses.why: modern usage loosened the legal core: two bodies can be partners without merging.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法松开了法律内核：两个机构不必合并也可以称伙伴。

senses.title: Two batters at one wicket
senses.titleCN: 板球中同时在场的一对击球手
senses.definition: in cricket, the pair batting together and the runs they add
senses.definitionCN: 板球中同时在场的两名击球手，以及他们共同取得的分数
senses.example: Their opening partnership added ninety runs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的开局搭档贡献了九十分。
senses.why: sport borrows the word for any pair that must cover for each other on the field.
senses.whyCN: 体育借这个词指任何在场上必须替对方补位的一对。

senses.title: A pairing at the card table
senses.definition: in card games, the pair who play as a team against other pairs
senses.definitionCN: 牌戏中作为一队对抗其他各对的两个人
senses.example: They have been a partnership at bridge for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在桥牌上做搭档已经三十年。
senses.why: a card pair must trust the other's unseen hand, which is partnership in its purest social form.
senses.whyCN: 一对牌手必须信赖对方看不见的牌，这是「合伙」最纯粹的社会形态。

senses.title: Shared responsibility in policy
senses.definition: an arrangement in which government, employers and workers share duties
senses.definitionCN: 政府、雇主与劳动者分担责任的一种安排
senses.example: The wage deal rested on a social partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工资协议建立在社会伙伴关系之上。
senses.why: politics uses the word for duties shared across sectors, where no contract binds the parties.
senses.whyCN: 政治用这个词指跨部门分担的责任，那里并没有合同约束各方。

senses.title: A legally recognised couple
senses.definition: a civil partnership giving a couple rights similar to marriage
senses.definitionCN: 给予一对伴侣类似婚姻权利的民事伴侣关系
senses.example: The law allowed a civil partnership from that year.
senses.exampleCN: 从那一年起，法律允许登记民事伴侣关系。
senses.why: the word spread from commerce to domestic life because both rest on a formal sharing of assets and duties.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从商业扩展到家庭生活，因为两者都建立在正式共享财产与责任之上。

senses.title: A coalition of parties
senses.definition: a governing arrangement between political parties that share power
senses.definitionCN: 分享权力的政党之间的执政安排
senses.example: The coalition called itself a partnership of equals.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联合政府自称是平等者之间的伙伴关系。
senses.why: coalitions borrow the commercial word to sound voluntary, since no party was bought.
senses.whyCN: 联合政府借用商业词，是为了听起来出于自愿，因为并没有哪一党被买下。

intro.en: Partnership is partner plus -ship, an Old English ending for a state or a body. Partner came from Old French parçonier, a sharer, from Latin partitio 'a division'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: partnership 是 partner 加 -ship 构成，后者是古英语中表示状态或团体的词尾。partner 来自古法语 parçonier「分有者」，源头是拉丁 partitio「分割」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pars meant 'a part, a share'. From it come partition, particle and the whole family of English part words.
items.cn: pars 意为「一部分、一份」。partition、particle 以及英语中整个 part 词族都由此而来。

items.en: Partitio, from partire 'to divide', named a dividing or a share, and Old French turned it into parçon.
items.cn: partitio 出自 partire「分割」，命名分割或所分得的一份，古法语把它变成 parçon。

items.en: Parçonier meant 'a sharer, one who has a part', and English borrowed it as partner in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: parçonier 意为「分有者、占一份的人」，英语在十三世纪以 partner 的形式借入。

items.en: The Old English ending -scipe marked state or condition, as in friendship and lordship; added to partner it made partnership around 1400.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -scipe 标记状态或情形，如 friendship 与 lordship；加在 partner 上，约在十五世纪初形成 partnership。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word hardened into a legal form of business, with deeds, liability and dissolution.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词固化为一种法律上的企业形式，有了契约、责任与解散程序。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first citation of partnership varies between dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of pars is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对 partnership 最早的用例说法不一；pars 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words on the same part root or on confusing near-forms; group two holds nouns for people or bodies that work as one.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「部分」词根、或形近易混的词；第二组收表示「作为一体运作的人或团体」的名词。

entries.definition: From Latin partitio: a division or a dividing screen, which is the physical act of what partnership shares.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 partitio：分割或隔板，正是 partnership 所「分有」的那个动作本身。

entries.definition: From Italian parte, a faction: a committed supporter of one side, sharing the root but not the mutual duty.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 parte「派别」：某一方的坚定支持者，同根，却不含相互的责任。

entries.definition: A sharer in an enterprise; partnership is the state or the body formed by such sharers.
entries.definitionCN: 共同经营中的分有者；partnership 则是由这些分有者形成的状态或团体。

entries.definition: A rarer form with co-, used mostly in older commercial writing for the same arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 加 co- 的较罕形式，多见于较早的商业文书，指同一种安排。

entries.definition: A union of separate parties for a purpose; it stresses remaining separate more than sharing ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种目的把各自独立的两方联合起来；更强调「仍然分开」，而非共享所有权。

entries.definition: A single business project shared by two firms; a partnership may run many projects over years.
entries.definitionCN: 两家公司共担的单一商业项目；而 partnership 可能持续多年、涵盖多个项目。

entries.definition: A separate legal entity; partners are personally liable, which a company's owners are not.
entries.definitionCN: 独立的法律实体；合伙人承担个人责任，而公司的所有者不承担。

entries.definition: A group of people organized around a shared interest; it need not trade or share profit.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕共同兴趣组织起来的一群人；它不必经商，也不必分利。

definition_zh: 一段文字；通道；过道；航程；通过
definition_en: a short section of a text or a piece of music, a narrow way through or along something, a journey by sea or air, or the process of a law being approved
core_image: 一条窄廊从两堵石墙之间穿过，尽头透出一线光
scene: 老城的巷子窄得只容一人通过，石墙上还留着旧日的门框。A narrow passage led from the street into a quiet courtyard.
sceneCN: 这里的 passage 是「通道、过道」（第 2 个义项：穿过建筑或墙壁的窄路）；句意为一条窄通道从街道通向安静的院子。图中可辨识物件：石墙、门框、巷口的光。

pos.zh: 一段文字；通道；过道；航程；通过

derivatives.zh: 由 passage 与 way 复合而成，义为「通道；走廊」
与 passage 同出拉丁语 passus（一步）与俗拉丁语 passare，是这一族词的基础动词，义为「经过；通过」
由 pass 加 -er 与 by 复合而成，义为「路过的人；行人」

senses.title: A short section of a text or a piece of music
senses.definition: a short part of a book, poem, speech or piece of music, considered on its own
senses.definitionCN: 书、诗、演讲或乐曲中单独拿出来看的一小部分
senses.example: She read the passage aloud to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这一段朗读给全班听。
senses.why: Passage first meant the act of going through, so a stretch of writing is pictured as a stretch of road that a reader travels from one end to the other.
senses.whyCN: passage 最早指「穿过去」这个动作，所以一段文字被想成一段路，读者从这头走到那头。

senses.title: A narrow way through or along something
senses.definition: a narrow way that lets a person move through a building, between walls or along a corridor
senses.definitionCN: 让人穿过建筑、墙与墙之间或沿走廊行走的窄路
senses.example: A narrow passage led from the street into a quiet courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄通道从街道通向安静的院子。
senses.why: The word names the act of passing, and the place that makes passing possible borrows the same name: a passage is where the going-through happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指「通过」这个动作，而让通过成为可能的那段空间就借用了同一个名字：passage 就是「穿过去」发生的地方。

senses.title: A journey, especially by sea or air
senses.definition: a journey from one place to another, especially by ship, and also the fare paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的行程，尤指乘船，也指为此支付的船费
senses.example: The storm made the passage across the channel dangerous.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使横渡海峡的航程变得危险。
senses.why: A voyage is simply a long act of passing from one shore to another, so the noun for going through extends to the whole crossing and to the money it costs.
senses.whyCN: 一次航行不过是从一片岸到另一片岸的漫长「穿过」，于是表示穿过的名词扩展到整段渡海行程，以及为它付出的钱。

senses.title: The process of a law being approved, or of time going by
senses.definition: the formal approval of a law by a legislature, or the movement of time from one moment to the next
senses.definitionCN: 立法机构对法律的正式通过，或时间从一刻走向下一刻
senses.example: The passage of the new law took almost a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新法几乎花了一年才通过。
senses.why: A bill must go through a series of stages before it becomes law, and time goes through the hours in the same way, so both are described with the noun of passing.
senses.whyCN: 一项法案必须走过一连串阶段才能成为法律，时间也同样一小时一小时地走过去，所以两者都用这个表示「通过」的名词。

intro.en: Passage goes back to Latin passus, a step, and the verb passare, to walk or cross, which French turned into passer and then into the noun passage.
intro.cn: passage 上溯拉丁语 passus（一步）与动词 passare（走、穿过），法语把它变成 passer，又造出名词 passage。

items.en: Pandere meant to spread or stretch out, and a leg stretched forward gives the family its first picture of movement.
items.cn: pandere 意为展开、伸开，一条腿向前伸出，给了这一族词最初的移动画面。

items.en: Passus named a single step and also a fixed length of ground measured in steps.
items.cn: passus 指单独的一步，也指以步为单位量出的固定长度。

items.en: The everyday verb passare meant to walk, to cross or to go through, and it is the source of the French verb.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语的动词 passare 意为走、越过、穿过，是法语动词的来源。

items.en: Old French made the noun passage for a crossing, a way through and a section of a text.
items.cn: 古法语造出名词 passage，指渡海、穿行的路，以及文本中的一段。

items.en: English borrowed passage in the thirteenth century and kept all three strands: the act of going through, the way itself, and a stretch of writing.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 passage，并保留了三条线索：通过的动作、通过的路，以及一段文字。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin step or merely spelled alike; the near-meaning group collects words for a way through and for a slice of a text.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个拉丁语「步」之上或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示通道与文本片段的词。

entries.definition: To go past or through something, or a document that lets you travel.
entries.definitionCN: 经过或穿过某物，也指准许通行的证件。

entries.definition: A corridor or narrow way that connects two places.
entries.definitionCN: 连接两处的走廊或窄路。

entries.definition: A person travelling in a vehicle; only the spelling is close, the sense is different.
entries.definitionCN: 乘车、乘船或乘飞机的人；只是拼写相近，词义不同。

entries.definition: A very strong feeling or a deep enthusiasm; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感或深切的爱好；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A long narrow space inside a building with doors on both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内部两侧有门的长窄空间；走廊。

entries.definition: A short piece taken from a book, film or piece of music.
entries.definitionCN: 从书、电影或乐曲中摘出的一小段。

entries.definition: A journey across water, or a place where a road or line can be crossed.
entries.definitionCN: 渡过水面的行程，或可以横穿的地方。

entries.definition: A short passage taken out of a longer text.
entries.definitionCN: 从较长文字中摘出的一段。

normalIntro.en: Passage keeps the picture of a step forward, and every sense is something a step can do: cross a room, cross a sea, cross a page, or carry a law to its end.
normalIntro.cn: passage 始终保留「向前一步」的画面，每个义项都是步子能做的事：穿过房间、穿过海面、穿过书页，或者把一项法案走到终点。

normal.en: Passage is pass plus the French ending -age, so the word says the act of passing before it says any place or text.
normal.cn: passage 是 pass 加法语词尾 -age，所以这个词先说的是「通过」这个动作，其次才是某处地方或某段文字。

normal.en: A passage in a building and a passage in a book share the idea of a stretch you travel along from one end to the other.
normal.cn: 建筑里的通道与书里的一段共享同一个想法：一段可以从头走到尾的路程。

normal.en: The passage of time and the passage of a bill both describe something moving through stages until it arrives.
normal.cn: 时间的流逝与法案的通过，都描述某物穿过一个个阶段，直到抵达终点。

normal.en: Passage is not the same as passenger: the first is the way or the trip, the second is the person carried along it.
normal.cn: passage 与 passenger 不同：前者是路或行程，后者是被带着走完这段路的人。

normal.en: Passion looks almost identical but comes from a Latin word for suffering, so the shared spelling is a coincidence of history.
normal.cn: passion 看起来几乎一样，却来自拉丁语中表示「受苦」的词，所以相同的拼写只是历史造成的巧合。

abstract.en: A single word for a corridor, a sea trip and a paragraph tells us that reading is also a kind of travel.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指走廊、海上行程与段落，说明阅读本身也是一种旅行。

abstract.en: A law passes the way a person passes a gate: it must be let through stage by stage, and each stage can stop it.
abstract.cn: 法律通过就像人过一道门：必须一关一关被放行，而每一关都可能把它拦下。

abstract.en: The passage of time is the one journey nobody can refuse, which is why the word sounds calm even when it describes loss.
abstract.cn: 时间的流逝是无人能拒绝的一段行程，所以这个词即使在说失去时，听上去也很平静。

examples.en: She read the passage aloud to the class.
examples.cn: 她把这一段朗读给全班听。

examples.en: A narrow passage led from the street into a quiet courtyard.
examples.cn: 一条窄通道从街道通向安静的院子。

examples.en: The passage of the new law took almost a year.
examples.cn: 这项新法几乎花了一年才通过。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a step that carries someone across; the senses divide into the way itself, the crossing, a stretch of writing read through, and a process carried to completion.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是带着人跨过去的一步；义项按「路本身」「渡过去」「读过去的一段文字」「走完全程的过程」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow corridor between two stone walls, a line of light at the far end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄廊从两堵石墙之间穿过，尽头透出一线光。

branches.en: a corridor with light at the far end
branches.cn: 尽头透着光的走廊

branches.en: a page read aloud in a classroom

branches.en: a ship pushing across a grey channel
branches.cn: 一条船顶着灰海横渡海峡

branches.en: a bill counted vote by vote
branches.cn: 逐票统计的一项法案

intro.en: The word joins a Latin noun for a step, a Latin verb for crossing, and a French noun ending that names an action or its result.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 passus 与 passare 均有记录，因此 passage 的世系直到法语阶段都是可靠的。

definition_zh: 乘客；旅客；随行者；旅鸽
definition_en: a person who travels in a vehicle but is not driving or working on it, a person who takes no active part in something, or the extinct migratory pigeon of North America
core_image: 渡轮甲板上挤满拎着行李的人，海风把衣角吹得鼓起
scene: 清晨的渡轮刚离岸，甲板上的人扶着栏杆看城市退远。Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
sceneCN: 这里的 passenger 是「乘客、旅客」（第 1 个义项：乘坐交通工具的人）；句意为渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。图中可辨识物件：栏杆、行李、海面。

derivatives.zh: 与 passenger 同出古法语 passager（过往的），后受 passage 影响改写词形，义为「航程；一段文字」
这一族词的基础动词，来自拉丁语 passus（一步），义为「经过；通过」
由 passenger 与 mile 复合而成，是运输业统计客运量的单位「客英里」

senses.title: A person travelling in a vehicle
senses.definition: a person who is travelling in a car, bus, train, ship or plane and is not the one operating it
senses.definitionCN: 乘坐汽车、公共汽车、火车、轮船或飞机，但不负责驾驶的人
senses.example: Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。
senses.why: The word began as the adjective passager, meaning passing or fleeting, and then named the person who makes a passage; a traveller carried by someone else is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是形容词 passager，意为「过往的、短暂的」，随后用来指走完一段行程的人；被人带着走的旅人正是这个意思。

senses.title: Someone who takes no active part
senses.definition: a person who is carried along by others and takes no active part or responsibility in what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 被别人带着走、对正在发生的事既不参与也不负责的人
senses.example: He felt like a passenger in his own company, watching others make every decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己在自己公司里只是个随行者，看着别人做所有决定。
senses.why: Since a passenger is the one who sits still while another drives, the word easily shifts from a seat on a bus to a seat in a meeting where someone else steers.
senses.whyCN: 乘客就是别人开车时坐着不动的那个人，所以这个词很容易从公交车上的座位，挪到由别人掌舵的会议里的座位。

senses.title: The extinct North American migratory pigeon
senses.definition: a gregarious pigeon of North America that migrated in huge flocks and became extinct in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 一种成群迁徙的北美鸽子，在二十世纪初灭绝
senses.example: The passenger pigeon once darkened the sky in flocks of millions.
senses.exampleCN: 旅鸽曾以数百万只成群飞过，把天空都遮暗了。
senses.why: The bird was named for its habit of passing through in vast migrating flocks, so the same idea of passing travellers gave the species its English name.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟因成百万只迁徙过境而得名，于是「过往的旅人」这同一个想法，给了这个物种它的英文名。

intro.en: Passenger derives from Old French passager, a traveller and also an adjective meaning passing, and its modern spelling was reshaped under the influence of passage.
intro.cn: passenger 源自古法语 passager，既指旅人，也是意为「过往的」的形容词；现代拼写是在 passage 的影响下改成这样的。

items.en: Passus, a step, and the verb passare, to cross, stand at the head of the family.
items.cn: passus（一步）与动词 passare（穿过）位于这一族词的最上游。

items.en: Old French passager meant both a traveller and something passing or brief.
items.cn: 古法语 passager 既指旅人，也指过往的、短暂的事物。

items.en: English took the word as passager, a person who makes a passage or a journey.
items.cn: 英语把它收作 passager，指走完一段行程或旅程的人。

items.en: The spelling gained an n, probably by association with passage, and became passenger.
items.cn: 拼写多出一个 n，可能是因为受了 passage 的类推，于是写成 passenger。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative sense of a person who takes no part, and keeps the name of the extinct passenger pigeon.
items.cn: 现代英语加上「不参与其中的人」这一比喻义，并保留了已灭绝的旅鸽之名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pass or merely spelled alike; the near-meaning group collects words for people who travel.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 pass 之上或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示出行者的词。

entries.definition: To go past something, or a permit to travel.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某物，或通行证。

entries.definition: A way through, a journey, or a part of a text.
entries.definitionCN: 通道、航程，或文本的一段。

entries.definition: An official document that lets you travel abroad; the second element is port, not a form of pass.

entries.definition: A very strong feeling or enthusiasm; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感或爱好；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person who is making a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 正在旅行的人。

entries.definition: A person who travels regularly between home and work.
entries.definitionCN: 定期往返于家与工作地点之间的人。

entries.definition: A person who travels on a horse, bicycle or bus.

entries.definition: A paying passenger, or the money paid for a journey.
