normalIntro.en: Passenger is a traveller word that has been reshaped by the word for the trip, so its hooks follow the person being carried rather than the driving.
normalIntro.cn: passenger 是一个表示旅人的词，被「行程」这个词改过形，所以记忆钩子跟着「被带着走的人」，而不是开车的人。

normal.en: Passenger comes from Old French passager, a traveller, and the extra n came later under the influence of passage.
normal.cn: passenger 来自古法语 passager（旅人），多出来的 n 是后来受 passage 影响才加上的。

normal.en: The opposite of a passenger is the driver: one is carried, the other does the carrying.
normal.cn: 乘客的对立面是司机：一个被带着走，一个负责带人走。

normal.en: Passenger seat is the seat beside the driver, named from the person who usually sits there.
normal.cn: passenger seat 是司机旁边的座位，因常坐在那里的人而得名。

normal.en: The passenger pigeon was named for passing through in huge migrating flocks, not for carrying anyone.
normal.cn: 旅鸽因成百万只迁徙过境而得名，并不是因为它载过谁。

normal.en: Passport looks related but its second half is port, a harbour, so the two words only share a beginning.
normal.cn: passport 看起来相关，但它的后半部分是 port（港口），两个词只是开头相同。

abstract.en: A passenger is proof that progress is often made by someone else, which is why the word can sound grateful or helpless.
abstract.cn: 乘客的存在说明前进常常是别人完成的，所以这个词听起来既可能带着感激，也可能带着无力。

abstract.en: Being called a passenger in your own life is a quiet complaint: the vehicle moves, but your hands are not on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 在自己的人生里被叫作乘客，是一句安静的抱怨：车在走，但方向盘不在你手上。

abstract.en: A bird named after passing shows that a whole species can be remembered by one habit of movement.
abstract.cn: 一种因「过境」而得名的鸟说明：整个物种可以被一个移动的习惯记住。

examples.en: Every passenger on the ferry watched the harbour shrink behind them.
examples.cn: 渡轮上的每位乘客都看着港口在身后缩小。

examples.en: He felt like a passenger in his own company, watching others make every decision.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己在自己公司里只是个随行者，看着别人做所有决定。

examples.en: The passenger pigeon once darkened the sky in flocks of millions.
examples.cn: 旅鸽曾以数百万只成群飞过，把天空都遮暗了。

root: 来自古法语 passager（旅人，也指「过往的」），其词根为拉丁语 passus（一步）与 passare（穿过）；现代拼写受 passage 影响加入 n，并非另有一个新词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person carried along by someone else's movement; the senses divide into the traveller, the figure who takes no part, and the bird that passes in flocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被别人的移动带着走的人；义项按「旅人」「不参与其中的人」「成群过境的鸟」分出。

branches.en: a deck crowded with coats and bags

branches.cn: 在舷梯口被查验的一张票

branches.en: a meeting where one person only listens
branches.cn: 一个人只带耳朵的一场会议

branches.en: a car moving while the hands stay still
branches.cn: 双手不动而车在前进

branches.en: a sky darkened by a migrating flock
branches.cn: 被迁徙鸟群遮暗的天空

intro.en: The word is a French traveller noun built on the Latin step, reshaped by the noun for the crossing, so its parts still say a person on a journey.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「一步」之上的法语旅人名词，又被表示「渡海」的名词改过形，各部分至今仍在说「在旅途中的人」。

latinIntro.en: Latin passus and passare are recorded, and the French forms descend from them, so the ancestry is reliable up to the spelling change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 passus 与 passare 均有记录，法语形式由它们而来，因此直到拼写变化之前，世系都是可靠的。

items.meaningCN: 护照；后半为 port（港口），与 passenger 只是开头相同

definition_zh: 激情；酷爱；强烈的情感；受难；盛怒
definition_en: a very strong feeling such as love or anger, a deep enthusiasm for something, the suffering of Christ in Christian teaching, or an old use for a fit of rage
core_image: 一个人伏在琴上，指尖用力，肩膀随旋律微微发抖
scene: 深夜的琴房里，一个人反复弹同一段旋律，额前的头发被汗粘住。She played the sonata with a passion that surprised her teacher.
sceneCN: 这里的 passion 是「激情、强烈的情感」（第 1 个义项：强烈的情感）；句意是她以连老师都吃惊的激情演奏这首奏鸣曲。图中可辨识物件：琴键、乐谱、台灯。

pos.zh: 激情；酷爱；强烈的情感；受难；盛怒

collocations.zh: 情杀；因情感冲动犯下的罪

derivatives.zh: 由 passion 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「热情的；激烈的」
由 passionate 加 -ly 构成，义为「热烈地；激烈地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 passionate 构成，义为「冷静的；不带感情的」
由 passion 加 -less（无）构成，义为「冷漠的；缺乏激情的」

senses.title: A very strong feeling
senses.definition: a very strong feeling, such as love, anger or grief, that takes hold of a person
senses.definitionCN: 抓住一个人的强烈情感，如爱、愤怒或悲痛
senses.example: She played the sonata with a passion that surprised her teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她以连老师都吃惊的激情演奏这首奏鸣曲。
senses.why: Passion comes from a Latin word for suffering, so the noun first named what a person undergoes; strong feeling was seen as something that happens to you rather than something you choose.
senses.whyCN: passion 来自拉丁语中表示「受苦」的词，所以这个名词最初指人「承受」的东西；强烈情感被看成发生在你身上的事，而不是你挑选的事。

senses.title: A deep enthusiasm for something
senses.definition: an intense and lasting enthusiasm for an activity or subject, or the activity itself
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动或主题持久而强烈的热情，也指这项活动本身
senses.example: His passion for old maps began in a dusty second-hand bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他对旧地图的酷爱始于一家满是灰尘的二手书店。
senses.why: If strong feeling can seize a person, it can also fasten on an object, and the thing so loved becomes the passion itself, which is why people speak of their passions as hobbies.
senses.whyCN: 既然强烈情感能抓住一个人，它也能牢牢附着在一个对象上，被如此热爱的东西本身就成了 passion，所以人们把自己热衷的爱好直接叫作 passions。

senses.title: The suffering of Christ
senses.definition: in Christian teaching, the suffering and death of Christ, especially as told in the Gospels
senses.definitionCN: 基督教教义中基督的受苦与死亡，尤指福音书所记
senses.example: The church holds a service to remember the Passion during Holy Week.
senses.exampleCN: 教会在圣周举行礼拜，纪念基督受难。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of all: the Latin noun simply meant suffering, and the Gospel accounts of Christ's final days kept that plain meaning alive in English.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一个义项：拉丁语名词本义就是「受苦」，福音书对基督最后几天的记述，让这个朴素的意思在英语里保存下来。

senses.title: A fit of rage
senses.definition: a sudden outburst of anger, used in older English especially in the phrase fly into a passion
senses.definitionCN: 突然爆发的愤怒，用于较早的英语，尤见于 fly into a passion 一语
senses.example: He flew into a passion when the clerk questioned his account.
senses.exampleCN: 店员质疑他的账目时，他勃然大怒。
senses.why: Because passion meant any strong feeling that takes you over, anger was one of its faces, and an outburst of anger was described as being seized by a passion.
senses.whyCN: 因为 passion 指任何一种占据你的强烈情感，愤怒也是它的一个面孔，所以一次暴怒就被说成被一股 passion 攫住。

intro.en: Passion descends from the Latin verb pati, to suffer, through the late Latin noun passio and Old French passion; the emotional senses grew out of the idea of being acted upon.
intro.cn: passion 由拉丁语动词 pati（受苦）经晚期拉丁语名词 passio 与古法语 passion 传下；那些情感义都是从「被作用于身」这一想法长出来的。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, to endure or to undergo, and it is the root shared with patience and passive.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、忍受、承受，是与 patience、passive 共有的词根。

items.en: Late Latin passio named suffering or a condition one undergoes; Christian writers used it for the suffering of Christ.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 passio 指受苦或人所承受的处境；基督教作者用它指基督的受难。

items.en: Old French passion carried both the religious sense and the wider sense of a strong emotion.
items.cn: 古法语 passion 同时带有宗教义与更宽泛的强烈情感义。

items.en: Middle English passion kept the religious sense first, then widened to love, grief and anger.
items.cn: 中古英语的 passion 最初保留宗教义，后来扩展到爱、悲痛与愤怒。

items.en: Modern English adds the everyday sense of an eager hobby, and keeps older idioms such as fly into a passion.
items.cn: 现代英语加上「热衷的爱好」这一日常义，并保留 fly into a passion 这类较早的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the Latin root for suffering or merely look alike; the near-meaning group collects words for intense feeling.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「受苦」词根或只是长得像的词；近义组收表示强烈情感的词。

entries.definition: Receiving an action rather than doing it; built on the same Latin verb pati.
entries.definitionCN: 承受动作而非发出动作；同出拉丁语 pati。

entries.definition: The ability to wait or endure without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 能够等待或忍受而不抱怨的能力。

entries.definition: Sympathy for the suffering of others, literally suffering with them.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的同情，字面义是「与之一同受苦」。

entries.definition: A way through or a section of a text; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 通道或文本的一段；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Intense enjoyment or interest in something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的强烈喜爱或兴趣。

entries.definition: Great energy or determination for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项事业投入的巨大热情或决心。

entries.definition: Very strong and sincere feeling, especially of belief.
entries.definitionCN: 极其强烈而真挚的感情，尤指信念。

entries.definition: Intense feeling of love or devotion, often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的爱意或献身之情，多用于文学。

normalIntro.en: Passion is built on a Latin verb for suffering, so every sense keeps the idea that a strong feeling is something a person undergoes rather than chooses.
normalIntro.cn: passion 建立在拉丁语表示「受苦」的动词之上，所以每个义项都保留一个想法：强烈情感是人承受的，而不是挑选的。

normal.en: Passion, patience, passive and compassion all come from Latin pati, to suffer, so the family is about what is done to you.
normal.cn: passion、patience、passive 与 compassion 都来自拉丁语 pati（受苦），所以这一族词说的都是「落到你身上的事」。

normal.en: The religious sense is the oldest: the Passion is what Christ underwent, not what he enjoyed.
normal.cn: 宗教义最古老：the Passion 是基督所承受的，而不是他所享受的。

normal.en: A passion for a hobby keeps the same shape: the interest takes hold of the person instead of the person holding it.
normal.cn: 对爱好的 passion 保持同一形状：是兴趣抓住了人，而不是人抓住了兴趣。

normal.en: Passion and enthusiasm are close, but passion is hotter and can include suffering, while enthusiasm is more often cheerful.
normal.cn: passion 与 enthusiasm 很近，但 passion 更炽烈，也可能带着痛苦，而 enthusiasm 通常更明朗。

normal.en: The idiom fly into a passion is old-fashioned; modern speakers usually say fly into a rage.
normal.cn: fly into a passion 这个说法已经过时，现代人多说 fly into a rage。

abstract.en: A word for suffering becoming a word for love suggests that deep feeling and pain were once thought to be the same event.
abstract.cn: 一个表示受苦的词变成了表示爱的词，说明深沉的情感与痛苦曾被看成同一件事。

abstract.en: We say a passion takes hold of us, never that we take hold of it, and that grammar quietly admits how little choice is involved.
abstract.cn: 我们说激情抓住了我们，从不说我们抓住了激情，这个语法细节悄悄承认了其中选择何其之少。

abstract.en: The Passion in a church and a passion for music share one root, which is why devotion can sound like a kind of endurance.
abstract.cn: 教堂里的受难与对音乐的酷爱共用一个词根，所以虔诚听起来可以像一种忍耐。

examples.en: She played the sonata with a passion that surprised her teacher.
examples.cn: 她以连老师都吃惊的激情演奏这首奏鸣曲。

examples.en: His passion for old maps began in a dusty second-hand bookshop.
examples.cn: 他对旧地图的酷爱始于一家满是灰尘的二手书店。

examples.en: He flew into a passion when the clerk questioned his account.
examples.cn: 店员质疑他的账目时，他勃然大怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派神」——派神一投入就忘我，像被什么附了身；记住 passion 是激情、酷爱。

root: 来自拉丁语 pati（受苦、承受），经晚期拉丁语 passio（受苦）与古法语 passion 进入英语；与 patience、passive 同根，词义由「所受之苦」扩展到一切强烈情感。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something a person undergoes; the senses divide into strong feeling in general, an enduring enthusiasm, the suffering of Christ, and the old sense of a burst of anger.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是人承受的东西；义项按「一般的强烈情感」「持久的酷爱」「基督受难」「旧用法中的暴怒」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person bent over a piano, fingers pressing hard, shoulders trembling with the melody.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人伏在琴上，指尖用力，肩膀随旋律微微发抖。

branches.cn: 敲在琴键上过重的一双手

branches.cn: 因情感过盛而无言的一张脸

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for suffering plus a noun ending for a state, so its parts say a condition that a person is put in.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「受苦」的动词加上表示状态的名词词尾构成，各部分说的是「人被打入的一种处境」。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati and passio are both recorded, and the English word follows them closely, so its Latin ancestry is reliable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 与 passio 均有记录，英语词紧紧跟随它们，因此其拉丁世系是可靠的。

items.meaningCN: 由 com-（共同）加 passio 构成，义为「同情」
